In a pair, giving that lands on the pair's own standings leaves levels and lines as no giving does while both stand; it decides who goes on only at an uneven shortfall, where there is slack and a renewal that reads standing (one built example), and it can also end the giver.

laws.name: PairFlow.levels_agree_until / levels_agree
laws.statement: theorem levels_agree {L₁ L₂ : Flow F C} {W₁ W₂ : Web F C} (b₁ : L₁.Balances W₁) (b₂ : L₂.Balances W₂) (start : ∀ c, W₁.level 0 c = W₂.level 0 c) (net : ∀ t, (∀ c, W₁.level t c = W₂.level t c) → ∀ c, L₁.taken t c + L₂.given t c = L₂.taken t c + L₁.given t c) : ∀ t c, W₁.level t c = W₂.level t c. levels_agree_until: the same with `net` asked only for t < T and the conclusion for t ≤ T.
laws.says: Two balanced flows from the same levels, whose takes and gives on each condition differ only by amounts that cancel at every step at which the levels still agree, keep the same levels. It speaks of levels only, not of activity, support or who gives.

laws.name: PairFlow.factors_equal
laws.statement: (same : ∀ t, t ≤ n → ∀ c, W₁.level t c = W₂.level t c) (read : (Nat → C → Nat) → Nat) (respects : ∀ l l', (∀ t, t ≤ n → ∀ c, l t c = l' t c) → read l = read l') (npos : 0 < n) (giving : read W₁.level = a + β * n) (withholding : read W₂.level = a + γ * n) : β = γ
laws.says: A reading of offspring that depends only on the levels up to step n gives two courses with the same levels the same number, so the two factors are equal.

laws.name: PairFlow.met_needs_within_start
laws.statement: theorem met_needs_within_start {L : Flow F C} {W : Web F C} (balances : L.Balances W) (own : F → C) (fs : List F) {S : Nat} (N : Nat) (gainless : ∀ t, S ≤ t → t < S + N → L.GainlessOn (fs.map own) t) : total fs (metNeed W own (S + N)) ≤ W.stock (fs.map own) S
laws.says: In a balanced flow, over a stretch at every step of which the family of the formations' own conditions gains nothing from any formation, the needs met at the end total at most the family's stock at the start. No giving within a closed family supports more need than it held.

laws.name: PairFlow.Routes (Parts, flow, web, balances, supported, line_offspring)
laws.statement: theorem balances : (flow P g).Balances (web P g) (any Parts P, any g : Pair → Nat → Bool). theorem supported (within : P.need ≤ P.stand) (t : Nat) (p : Pair) : (web P g).Supported t (member p). theorem line_offspring (s : Place) (n : Nat) : (web P (gaveIn s)).level n (line s.side) = s.offspring (P.start + P.own * n) (P.reach + P.matched) P.kept n. Definitions: level renewer = 0, level (member _) = P.stand, level (line p) = lineAt; the renewer gives `renewed` and takes 0.
laws.says: For any constant parts, a pair's run is a balanced flow in which a renewer that takes nothing gives each standing exactly what is drawn from it, so both standings are constant and supported by construction; the level of a formation's line is PairSelection's offspring formula with β = reach + matched and γ = kept. General over the parts, but the standings cannot run down and the line is an accumulator, not a formation.

laws.name: PairFlow.Routes.gap_iff / plain / signs
laws.statement: theorem gap_iff (routes : P.kept + P.spoiled = P.reach + P.spill) : P.kept < P.reach + P.matched ↔ P.spill < P.spoiled + P.matched. plain: with routes, spill = 0, spoiled = 0, matched = 0 the line is `s.offspring (P.start + P.own * n) P.reach P.reach n`. signs: by `decide`, perishing and matching have kept < reach + matched, carried has reach + matched < kept.
laws.says: Where what is kept is the gift's amount, a gift brings the receiver more than keeping brings the keeper exactly where giving loses less than keeping spoils together with what the renewer adds to each gift; with no loss and no matching the two are equal. `signs` is three built examples.

laws.name: PairFlow.WhileStanding.runs_agree_until
laws.statement: theorem runs_agree_until {S₁ S₂ : Setting} (giving : ∀ p t, S₁.intends p t = true) (withholding : ∀ p t, S₂.intends p t = false) (renew : ∀ p t, S₁.renew p t = S₂.renew p t) (draw : ∀ p t, S₁.draw p t = S₂.draw p t) (start : S₁.start = S₂.start) {T : Nat} (active : ∀ t, t < T → ∀ p, isActive G (levels G S₁ t) p = true) : ∀ t, t ≤ T → ∀ c, (web G S₁).level t c = (web G S₂).level t c. (G : Parts carries fits : ∀ p, upkeep + own + gift ≤ need p.)
laws.says: In the pair model with renewal while standing, a run in which both give at every step and a run in which neither does, with the same renewal offered, draws and start, have the same levels (standings and lines) up to T provided both formations are active at every step before T of the giving run. One-sided giving is not covered. It is levels_agree applied to two formations on two conditions.

laws.name: PairFlow.WhileStanding.stays_fallen
laws.statement: theorem stays_fallen {p : Pair} {t : Nat} (idle : isActive G (levels G S t) p = false) (none : ∀ s, t ≤ s → sends G S s (levels G S s) (partner p) = false) : ∀ d, standing (levels G S (t + d)) p ≤ standing (levels G S t) p ∧ isActive G (levels G S (t + d)) p = false
laws.says: In that model a formation below its need, to which its partner gives at no later step, never rises and is never active again. Near-definitional: the renewer gives only to an active formation.

laws.name: PairFlow.WhileStanding.lines_agree_while_active
laws.statement: theorem lines_agree_while_active {S₁ S₂ : Setting} (p : Pair) : ∀ n, (∀ t, t < n → isActive G (levels G S₁ t) p = isActive G (levels G S₂ t) p) → lineAt G S₁ p n = lineAt G S₂ p n
laws.says: A formation's line is the same in two runs in which it is active at the same steps, whatever the giving, renewal and draws: read this way, giving changes offspring only by changing who stands.

laws.name: PairFlow.FailedRenewal.lines_gain (with gifts_sharing, agree_to_shortfall)
laws.statement: theorem lines_gain (m : Nat) : lineAt parts sharing first (m + 4) + lineAt parts sharing second (m + 4) = lineAt parts keeping first (m + 4) + lineAt parts keeping second (m + 4) + m. Fixed data: needs 3 and 3; upkeep, line's part and gift 1 each; renewer offers 2 a step to each, 0 to the second at step 1; no outside draw; start (5, 3).
laws.says: One setting, for every length m + 4. What it needs: a renewer that takes nothing, requires nothing and gives only to a formation at or above its need; the first's two units of slack above its need; one failed renewal. Sharing, the first's two unreturned gifts lift the second back to its need and the renewer's giving to it resumes; keeping, the second never stands again. The first's line is n in both runs; all of the gain is the second's line. That the gain is the resumed inflow is read from the definitions, not stated by the theorem.

laws.name: PairFlow.GiverAtNeed.gift_lost / withholder_same / standings_differ
laws.statement: theorem gift_lost (m : Nat) : lineAt FailedRenewal.parts bothKeep first (m + 1) = lineAt FailedRenewal.parts giverAlone first (m + 1) + m. theorem withholder_same (n : Nat) : lineAt FailedRenewal.parts giverAlone second n = lineAt FailedRenewal.parts bothKeep second n.
laws.says: From standings at their needs (3, 3), a formation that gives one unit to one that never gives falls below its need and never stands again; its line is m short of what keeping leaves it, and the receiver's line is the same either way.

laws.name: PairSelection.Place.offspring
laws.statement: def offspring (a β γ n : Nat) (s : Place) : Nat := a + β * s.received n + γ * s.withheld n
laws.says: Offspring as a supplied formula: a base, β for each step the partner gave, γ for each step withheld. Giving here is a Bool course of a pair's laws; β and γ are supplied numbers, with no flow and no level.

laws.name: PairSelection.never_rises_in_pairs (with pair_le)
laws.statement: theorem never_rises_in_pairs {β γ : Nat} (le : β ≤ γ) (a n : Nat) {gs : List (List Place)} (paired : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∃ s, g = [s, s.other]) (others : ∀ s, s ∈ whole gs → s.kind = false → s.law s.side = withholding) : ¬ discord (whole gs) (Place.offspring a β γ n) (amountOf Place.kind) < concord (whole gs) (Place.offspring a β γ n) (amountOf Place.kind)
laws.says: With the supplied factors β ≤ γ, in any cohort listed as pairs in which every place not of the kind withholds, the kind is not selected for, whatever laws it holds and whatever the errors. On supplied factors, one generation.

laws.name: PairSelection.assorted_raises_iff (with assorted_counts)
laws.statement: theorem assorted_raises_iff {a β γ n : Nat} (pos : 0 < a) (npos : 0 < n) {x : CarrierCounts} (some : 0 < x.carrier) : x.carrier * (CarrierCounts.select x (shaped a (β * n) 0 (γ * n) pos)).other < (CarrierCounts.select x (shaped a (β * n) 0 (γ * n) pos)).carrier * x.other ↔ γ < β
laws.says: Under complete assortment (answerers paired with answerers, withholders with withholders) the pairs' offspring are RuleShaping's rule after shaping, and the answerers' share is raised strictly exactly where γ < β. Supplied factors.

laws.name: PairSelection.rise_le_slack_inflow and Place.received_factor_le / received_factor_zero
laws.statement: theorem rise_le_slack_inflow {L : Flow F C} {W : Web F C} (balances : L.Balances W) {dep : C → F} {ds rest : List C} {t β : Nat} (met : W.MetOn dep rest t) (unbroken : ∀ c, c ∈ rest → ¬ W.Broken t (dep c) c) (rise : W.stock ds (t + 1) = W.stock ds t + β) : β + L.lost (ds ++ rest) t ≤ W.slack dep rest t + L.inflow (ds ++ rest) t
laws.says: In a balanced flow, a family's rise across a step, with what the whole loses, is at most the slack of the dependences beyond it and the whole's inflow, unless a dependence beyond breaks. received_factor_le sums this over received steps under the hypothesis that the line rises by β at each; received_factor_zero: with no slack and no inflow at those steps, β = 0.

laws.name: PairSelection.Needs.asymmetry_gains / symmetry_moves
laws.statement: theorem asymmetry_gains : (web 1).Supported 0 giver ∧ ¬ (web 1).Supported 0 receiver ∧ (∀ t, (web 1).Supported (t + 1) giver ∧ (web 1).Supported (t + 1) receiver). theorem symmetry_moves : (web 2).Supported 0 giver ∧ ¬ (web 2).Supported 0 receiver ∧ (∀ t, ¬ (web 2).Supported (t + 1) giver ∧ (web 2).Supported (t + 1) receiver)
laws.says: A closed balanced pair, levels 2 and 1, one unit moved once. With needs 1 and 2 both end supported (the giver had slack one); with needs 2 and 2 the move only moves support.

laws.name: PairSelection.Renewed.renewal_carried (with renewer_free, inflow_one)
laws.statement: theorem renewal_carried : (∀ t, flow.give t giver receiver = 1 ∧ web.Supported t giver ∧ web.Supported t receiver ∧ web.level (t + 1) giver = web.level t giver) ∧ ∀ T N, total (steps T N) (fun t => flow.give t giver receiver) = N ∧ total (steps T N) (flow.inflow [giver, receiver]) = N. theorem renewer_free : ∀ t c, ¬ web.requires t renewer c.
laws.says: All levels constant at one. A renewer that takes nothing and requires nothing gives the giver one unit a step, the giver passes one to the receiver, and both stay supported for ever; what the giver gives over any stretch equals the inflow into the pair. The flow balances although the renewer's giving is drawn from nothing.

laws.name: SelectionLevels.rises_iff_kept (with within_kept, among_kept)
laws.statement: theorem rises_iff_kept (gs : List (List α)) (w a : α → Nat) {B s q K m : Nat} (equal : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → g.length = m) (returns : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∀ p, p ∈ g → w p + K * a p = B + s * a p + q * total g a) : discord (whole gs) w a < concord (whole gs) w a ↔ K * concord (whole gs) a a < s * concord (whole gs) a a + m * q * concordAmong gs a a. within_kept (same `returns`): concordWithin gs w a + K * concordWithin gs a a = discordWithin gs w a + s * concordWithin gs a a.
laws.says: For groups of equal size m, where each unit a member keeps costs it K, brings s back to it alone and gives q to every member of its group, the whole selects for keeping exactly where K times the whole's spread falls short of s times it with m·q times the spread among groups; within groups only s against K counts. An identity on lists of numbers: the returns are a hypothesis on the weights, and there is no flow, condition or level that could run down.

laws.name: SelectionLevels.rises_iff_returns_of_uniform / not_rises_of_alike
laws.statement: rises_iff_returns_of_uniform (equal) (returns : … w p + (b + c) * a p = B + b * total g a) (uniform : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∃ v, ∀ p, p ∈ g → a p = v) (differ : 0 < concordAmong gs a a) : discord (whole gs) w a < concord (whole gs) w a ↔ b + c < m * b. not_rises_of_alike (equal) (returns) (alike : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → total g a = d) : ¬ discord (whole gs) w a < concord (whole gs) w a.
laws.says: With nothing coming back to the keeper alone: groups uniform in the amount that differ select for it exactly where b + c < m·b; groups alike in their totals never select for it.

laws.name: SelectionLevels.rises_exact_iff_returns
laws.statement: (listed : whole gs = G.family t) (equal : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → g.length = m) (returns : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∀ p, p ∈ g → G.offspringNumber t p + (b + c) * G.amount t p = B + b * total g (G.amount t)) (exact : Exact (G.family t) (G.kids t) (G.amount t) (G.amount (t + 1))) : G.Raises t ↔ (b + c) * concord (G.family t) (G.amount t) (G.amount t) < m * b * concordAmong gs (G.amount t) (G.amount t)
laws.says: The same rule over listed generations, for one step t, with exact transmission and the returns assumed of the offspring numbers at that step. Generations are lists; no web.

laws.name: SelectionLevels.lineages_within_none / rises_iff_lineages
laws.statement: rises_iff_lineages (listed : whole gs = G.family 0) (exact : ∀ t, Exact …) (uniform : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∃ v, ∀ p, p ∈ g → G.amount 0 p = v) (c) (common : ∀ h, h ∈ lineages G gs t → h.length * c h = n) (pos : 0 < n) : G.Raises t ↔ discordMeans (lineages G gs t) c (G.offspringNumber t) (G.amount t) < concordMeans (lineages G gs t) c (G.offspringNumber t) (G.amount t)
laws.says: With groups formed by descent from groups uniform in the amount and exact transmission, nothing is selected within a lineage at any generation and the mean rises exactly as selection among the lineages' means goes. Lists only.

laws.name: SelectionLevels.Founding.either_verdict
laws.statement: discord (whole assorted) assortedOffspring keeps < concord (whole assorted) assortedOffspring keeps ∧ (2 + 1) * concord (whole assorted) keeps keeps = 12 ∧ 2 * 2 * concordAmong assorted keeps keeps = 16 ∧ concord (whole mixed) mixedOffspring keeps < discord (whole mixed) mixedOffspring keeps ∧ concordAmong mixed keeps keeps = 0 ∧ concordWithin mixed mixedOffspring keeps < discordWithin mixed mixedOffspring keeps
laws.says: Four members, two keepers, each unit kept giving two to its groupmate and taking one from the keeper: with the keepers in one group the whole selects for keeping, with one keeper in each group against it. A table of offspring numbers.

laws.name: Founding.Flow.survivors_independent
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {G : Generations X} (descended : SelectionTerm.Flow.Descended L W G) {ds : List X} {m : Nat} (gated : ∀ t f, f ∈ L.present t → ∀ d, d ∈ ds → 0 < L.give t f d → ∃ e, e ∈ ds ∧ W.requires t f e ∧ m ≤ W.need t f e) {T n : Nat} (excess : ∀ k, k < n → L.replenishment ds (T + k) < L.uptake ds (T + k)) (start : W.stock ds T < n + m) (k : Nat) {x : X} (mx : x ∈ G.family (T + n + k + 1)) : ∃ p, p ∈ G.family (T + n + k) ∧ x ∈ G.kids (T + n + k) p ∧ ∀ e, e ∈ ds → W.requires (T + n + k) p e → ¬ m ≤ W.need (T + n + k) p e
laws.says: On a balanced web where only active formations give and activity needs support, once a family of conditions whose givers all depend on it has had n steps of uptake above replenishment from a stock below n + m, every member of a later generation of descent is the offspring of a member that did not depend on the family at a need of m or more. The excess is a hypothesis.

laws.name: Founding.Flow.confined_ends (and ConfinedRise.ends)
laws.statement: Same premises as survivors_independent, with (founded : ∀ p, p ∈ h → p ∈ G.family 0) (confined : ∀ k p, p ∈ lineage G h (T + n + k) → ∃ e, e ∈ ds ∧ W.requires (T + n + k) p e ∧ m ≤ W.need (T + n + k) p e) (k : Nat) : lineage G h (T + n + k + 1) = []
laws.says: A lineage every member of which, from T + n on, depends on the overdrawn family has no member at any later generation. `Rise` also asks that selection within went for the lineage and that it drew on the family; those two clauses are not used in the proof.

laws.name: Founding.Nested.raises_iff_among (with raises_iff_carried)
laws.statement: theorem raises_iff_among {C : Nested α} (founded : C.Founded) (sequestered : C.Sequestered) (t : Nat) : C.wholes.Raises t ↔ C.wholes.discordAt t < C.wholes.concordAt t
laws.says: Where each whole has one founder and every next founder carries its founder's value, the mean founding value rises exactly where selection among wholes goes for it, whatever happened within. Generations as lists; no flow, no returns, no levels.

laws.name: Founding.Body (confined_rise, confined_ended, spread_rise, spread_unconfined, spread_outlasts)
laws.statement: theorem confined_ended (k : Nat) : lineage (generationsBy ofConfined) [confined] (0 + 1 + k + 1) = []. theorem spread_outlasts : lineage (generationsBy ofSpread) [spread] 2 = [spread₂].
laws.says: One body condition at level two, taken to nothing by two founders in one step, nothing giving to it. Both lineages meet every clause of a rise; the one whose offspring needs the body ends; the one whose offspring needs a condition outside it has a member one generation later, and none after that.

laws.name: GroupEnding.Flow.family_childless / ended_of_family / coupled_end_together / all_end
laws.statement: ended_of_family (balances) (acting) (dependent) (gated) (excess) (start) (k) (descended) (listed : whole gs = G.family (T + n + k)) (coupled : ∀ g h, g ∈ gs → h ∈ gs → total h a < total g a → ∀ p, p ∈ h → ∃ e, e ∈ ds ∧ W.requires (T + n + k) p e ∧ m ≤ W.need (T + n + k) p e) : Ended gs (G.offspringNumber (T + n + k)) a. coupled_end_together (same base premises) (within) (coupled : every member of every group so depends) (a) : (∀ h, h ∈ gs → total h (G.offspringNumber (T + n + k)) = 0) ∧ concordAmong gs (G.offspringNumber (T + n + k)) a = 0 ∧ discordAmong gs (G.offspringNumber (T + n + k)) a = 0. all_end (acting) (descended) (inactive : ∀ p, p ∈ G.family t → ¬ W.active t p) : G.size (t + 1) = 0.
laws.says: On a balanced web with descent: groups whose members depend on an overdrawn, self-gated family leave no offspring; if all groups depend on one such family they all leave none and nothing is selected among them; if only the groups with less of an amount do, nothing among groups goes against the amount. The account's "one shared condition" for all_end is a reading: the Lean hypothesis is only that every member is inactive.

laws.name: GroupEnding.Flow.lineages_raises
laws.statement: (acting : L.Acting W) (descended) (listed : whole gs = G.family 0) (exact : ∀ t, Exact …) (founded : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∀ p, p ∈ g → G.amount 0 p = v g) (inactive : ∀ g h, g ∈ gs → h ∈ gs → v h < v g → ∀ p, p ∈ lineage G h t → ¬ W.active t p) (mg) (mh) (less : v h < v g) (mp : p ∈ lineage G g t) (mq : q ∈ lineage G h t) (leaves : 0 < G.offspringNumber t p) : G.Raises t
laws.says: With lineages founded at values and exact transmission, where every lower-founded lineage's members are inactive at a step and a higher-founded member leaves offspring beside a lower one, the mean amount rises. Both the inactivity and the leaving of offspring are hypotheses.

laws.name: Reproduction.Flow.lineage_ends (with born_within_stock, closed_not_exact)
laws.statement: theorem lineage_ends {ds : List X} (descended : SelectionTerm.Flow.Descended L W G) (within : ∀ t p k, p ∈ G.family t → k ∈ G.kids t p → k ∈ ds) (balances : ∀ t, t < W.stock ds 0 + 1 → L.BalancesOn W ds t) (dissipates : ∀ t, t < W.stock ds 0 + 1 → L.DissipatesOn ds t) : G.size (W.stock ds 0 + 1) = 0
laws.says: Generations of descent whose offspring all stand within a family that is balanced and dissipated on (every formation gives it less than it takes when it takes) across each step up to the family's starting stock have an empty generation after those steps. It needs dissipation: a formation that only gives to the family breaks the premise.

laws.name: Reproduction.Relay.relay
laws.statement: theorem relay : flow.Balances web ∧ (∀ t, ¬ flow.DissipatesOn family t) ∧ SelectionTerm.Flow.Descended flow web generations ∧ ∀ n, generations.size n = 1 ∧ web.stock family n = 1
laws.says: Two relata pass one unit back and forth, losing nothing; the flow balances, the family is dissipated on at no step, and the lineage has one member at every generation for ever.

laws.name: CoupledDrawers gated_threshold, one_keeps_several_drain, gatedRenewal
laws.statement: def gatedRenewal (m q : Nat) (_ x : Nat) : Nat := if m ≤ x then x + q else x. theorem one_keeps_several_drain {q : Nat} (pos : 0 < m) (below : c < m) (keepingGains : 0 < c + q) : (∀ rules, Perfect (gatedRenewal m q) (fun _ _ _ => 0) rules 1 c m 2 → ∀ a, m ≤ a → m ≤ rules 0 0 a) ∧ (∀ k' rules, 1 < k' → Perfect (gatedRenewal m q) (fun _ _ _ => 0) rules k' c m 2 → ∀ t, t < 2 → ∀ d, d < k' → ∀ a, rules d t a = 0). gated_threshold (two : 1 < k) (pos : 0 < m): c < m → every perfect profile drains; c ≤ m → draining is perfect; m ≤ c → keeping the need is perfect; m < c → every perfect profile keeps exactly the need.
laws.says: Laws of best-responding drawers over a finite horizon on a level whose next value is a supplied function G of what is left; with two or more drawers in turn the threshold for keeping is the need itself, and one drawer keeps where several drain. The level's renewal `x + q` is a rule of the level with no giver: this module uses no Flow, Web or Balances, and has no descent or selection term.

laws.name: ReadOffInTime.stopped_is_regime (with balances)
laws.statement: theorem stopped_is_regime : ∀ k n, habitat k (n + stopAt k) = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step giving 1) (habitat k (stopAt k))).state n. theorem balances : ∀ k, (flow k).Balances (web k).
laws.says: Four fixed courses of a habitat on a balanced flow, with a dweller taking one unit and a renewer (takes nothing, requires nothing) giving one while the habitat stands at 2 or above; after the clearer stops, the habitat's level is the run of RegimeMargin's step with that giving and draw 1.

laws.name: Stock.stockFlow_balances
laws.statement: theorem stockFlow_balances {P : Process S A} {σ : S → Nat} {draw replenish : A → Nat} (bal : Stock.Balanced P σ draw replenish) (r : Run P) : (stockFlow r draw replenish).Balances (stockWeb r σ), where stockFlow r draw replenish : Flow Unit Unit := ⟨fun _ => [()], fun t _ _ => draw (r.act t), fun t _ _ => replenish (r.act t)⟩
laws.says: Any run of a process whose stock balances step by step is a balanced flow with one condition and one formation that takes the draw and gives the replenishment. By grep the four line modules do not use it.

laws.name: RuleShaping.grouped_rises_iff
laws.statement: theorem grouped_rises_iff {gs : List (List α)} {w shapes : α → Nat} {a s q c m : Nat} {pos : 0 < a} (equal : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → g.length = m) (grouped : Grouped gs w shapes a s q c pos) : discord (whole gs) w shapes < concord (whole gs) w shapes ↔ c * concord (whole gs) shapes shapes < s * concord (whole gs) shapes shapes + m * q * concordAmong gs shapes shapes := rises_iff_kept gs w shapes equal (grouped_returns grouped)
laws.says: The rule after shaping read in groups is SelectionLevels.rises_iff_kept with K = c; the proof is that one application.

That is drawn too strongly. `Flow.Balances` (Flow.lean:278) is one equation per condition: `W.level (t + 1) c + L.taken t c = W.level t c + L.given t c`. It attributes every change of a level to formations present; it puts no constraint on a formation. A formation may give at every step while taking nothing and requiring nothing, and the flow balances. My files do exactly this four times: PairSelection.Renewed (renewer, `renewer_free`, all levels constant at 1, PairSelection.lean:2052-2109), PairFlow.Routes (renewer at level 0 giving `renewed`, PairFlow.lean:252, 286, 306), PairFlow.WhileStanding (renewer at level 0 giving `renewal`, lines 497, 576), ReadOffInTime (renewer, lines 858, 871, 891). `Flow.inflow` (Entropy.lean:577) is a defined quantity and laws are graded by it. So the web names the outside as a formation; it does not make it rest on anything. laws.statement: def step (g : Nat → Nat) (H x : Nat) : Nat := (x - H) + g (x - H)

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Adjusted.step
laws.statement: def step (A : Nat → Nat → Nat) (H : Nat) (p : Nat × Nat) : Nat × Nat := (p.1 - H + A (p.1 - H) p.2, A (p.1 - H) p.2)
laws.says: The state is a level and what was given last; what is added is a function A of what the draw leaves and of what was given last.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.step
laws.statement: def step (g₁ g₂ : V → V → V) (H₁ H₂ : V) (p : V × V) : V × V := (D.add (D.sub p.1 H₁) (g₁ (D.sub p.1 H₁) (D.sub p.2 H₂)), D.add (D.sub p.2 H₂) (g₂ (D.sub p.1 H₁) (D.sub p.2 H₂)))
laws.says: Two conditions, each under its own standing draw. What is added to each is a function of what the draws leave of both. Nothing is taken from one condition to be given to the other: each loses only its own draw.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.step
laws.statement: def step (G : ι → (ι → V) → V) (H : ι → V) (x : ι → V) : ι → V := fun i => D.add (D.sub (x i) (H i)) (G i (left D H x)), with left H x = fun i => D.sub (x i) (H i) (:2109)
laws.says: Any number of conditions. Condition i's next level is what its draw leaves plus G i of what the draws leave of every condition. So a condition's giving is a function of what is left of the others, but the amount is not drawn from them.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.Recent.step
laws.statement: def step (G : ι → (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat) → Nat) (H : ι → Nat) (x : ι × Bool → Nat) : ι × Bool → Nat | (i, true) => (x (i, true) - H i) + G i (fun j => x (j, true) - H j) (fun j => x (j, false)) | (i, false) => G i (fun j => x (j, true) - H j) (fun j => x (j, false))
laws.says: Each condition carries its level and what it gave last. What is added to condition i is G i of what the draws leave of every condition and of what every condition gave last. Again no amount passes from one condition to another.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.step_mono
laws.statement: theorem step_mono {G : ι → (ι → V) → V} (rises : ∀ i, Rises D (G i)) (H : ι → V) {x y : ι → V} (below : Below D x y) : Below D (step D G H x) (step D G H y), with Rises g := ∀ e e', Below D e e' → D.le (g e) (g e') (:2120)
laws.says: Where every condition's giving does not fall as what is left of any condition rises, a state at or below another, condition by condition, stays so after a step. Any amounts with a draw.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.ends_of_below
laws.statement: theorem ends_of_below {G : ι → (ι → V) → V} {H : ι → V} {part : (ι → V) → V} (rises : ∀ i, Rises D (G i)) (reads : ∀ x y, Below D x y → D.le (part x) (part y)) {x y : ι → V} (below : Below D x y) (ends : Ends D G H part y) : Ends D G H part x
laws.says: Under that premise, a level that comes to nothing and stays there from a state does so from every state at or below it. Raising any condition never ends one that held.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.DependsOn, drains, ends_of_partner
laws.statement: def DependsOn (G) (i j : ι) : Prop := ∀ e : ι → V, e j = D.zero → G i e = D.zero. theorem drains (depends : DependsOn D G i j) {x} (within : D.le (x j) (H j)) : step D G H x i = D.sub (x i) (H i). theorem ends_of_partner {G : ι → (ι → Nat) → Nat} {H : ι → Nat} {i j : ι} (depends : DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j) (pos : 0 < H i) {s} (ends : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w j) s) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s
laws.says: Where condition i gives nothing whenever nothing is left of j, i only loses its draw once j is within its draw; in whole numbers, with i's draw positive, wherever j ends i ends.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.ends_downstream, ends_together
laws.statement: theorem ends_downstream {G : ι → (ι → Nat) → Nat} {H : ι → Nat} (pos : ∀ i j, DependsOn Drawn.whole G i j → 0 < H i) {s} : ∀ {i k : ι}, Downstream Drawn.whole G i k → Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w k) s → Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s. theorem ends_together (pos : same) {s} {i k} (there : Downstream Drawn.whole G i k) (back : Downstream Drawn.whole G k i) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w i) s ↔ Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun w => w k) s
laws.says: In whole numbers, where every condition that depends on another has a positive draw, the end of one ends everything along any chain of dependence from it, and two conditions each downstream of the other end together or not at all.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.within_draw, left_falls
laws.statement: theorem within_draw (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) {hi : Nat} (band : Band G H hi) {x : ι → Nat} (high : ∀ i, x i ≤ hi) (i : ι) : G i (left Drawn.whole H x) ≤ H i. theorem left_falls (rises) (band : Band G H hi) {s} (high : ∀ i, s i ≤ hi) (n : Nat) (i : ι) : (Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) s).state (n + 1) i - H i ≤ (Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) s).state n i - H i
laws.says: Where giving does not fall as what is left rises and the step keeps every level up to hi within hi, each condition gives at most its own draw, and what the draws leave of each never rises along a run.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.comes_to_rest
laws.statement: theorem comes_to_rest (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) {hi : Nat} (band : Band G H hi) {cs : List ι} (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) {s : ι → Nat} (high : ∀ i, s i ≤ hi) : ∃ N, N ≤ cs.length * hi + 1 ∧ ∀ k i, (Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) s).state (N + k) i = (Law.run (step Drawn.whole G H) s).state N i
laws.says: Finitely many conditions under those two premises: the run is still from some step at most the number of conditions times hi, plus one. Its proof (rests_by, :2577) uses Amounts.unmarked_within on the total of what the draws leave; that is a count balanced against nothing given, not Flow.Balances on a web.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.ends_iff_below, threshold_falls
laws.statement: theorem ends_iff_below [DecidableEq ι] (rises : ∀ i, Rises Drawn.whole (G i)) {hi} (band : Band G H hi) {cs} (covers : ∀ i, i ∈ cs) {y : ι → Nat} {i : ι} {a : Nat} (high : a ≤ hi) (highs : ∀ j, y j ≤ hi) : Ends Drawn.whole G H (fun x => x i) (setAt y i a) ↔ a < threshold G H cs hi y i. theorem threshold_falls (rises) (band) (covers) {y y'} {i} (le : ∀ j, y j ≤ y' j) (highs' : ∀ j, y' j ≤ hi) : threshold G H cs hi y' i ≤ threshold G H cs hi y i
laws.says: Under the same premises each condition has, given the other levels, a least level below which exactly it ends, and that level does not rise as any other condition's level rises. Beyond a band the same holds for any law keeping the order of states where the run stays within a bound (ends_iff_below_within :2984, threshold_falls_within :2997).

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.Relay.cycles
laws.statement: theorem cycles : Drawn.whole.Rises first ∧ Drawn.whole.Rises second ∧ (∀ a, first a 0 = 0) ∧ (∀ b, second 0 b = 0) ∧ (∀ x, Ends Drawn.whole first second 1 1 Prod.fst (x, 0)) ∧ (∀ y, Ends Drawn.whole first second 1 1 Prod.snd (0, y)) ∧ (∀ n, ((Law.run (step Drawn.whole first second 1 1) (2, 3)).state n).1 ≤ 3 ∧ (…).2 ≤ 3) ∧ ¬ Ends … Prod.fst (2, 3) ∧ ¬ Ends … Prod.snd (2, 3) ∧ ∀ N, ¬ LastChange.StillFrom (Law.run (step Drawn.whole first second 1 1) (2, 3)) N, with first a b = if 1 ≤ a ∧ 2 ≤ b then 2 else 0, second a b = if 2 ≤ a ∧ 1 ≤ b then 2 else 0
laws.says: Two conditions each of which ends alone from every level; from two and three the pair moves between (2,3) and (3,2) for ever under draws of one each. Each step two are drawn and two are added, by the giving functions; no formation gives them.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.MutualActivation.saves; MutualInhibition.breaks_order; Indexed.Chain.cascades, stopped
laws.statement: saves: … Ends Drawn.whole giving giving 1 1 Prod.fst (2, 0) ∧ ¬ Ends Drawn.whole giving giving 1 1 Prod.fst (2, 2) ∧ threshold giving giving 1 1 2 0 = 3 ∧ threshold giving giving 1 1 2 2 = 2. breaks_order: ¬ Drawn.whole.Rises first ∧ … ∧ threshold first second 1 1 2 0 = 2 ∧ threshold first second 1 1 2 2 = 3. cascades: DependsOn … giving 2 1 ∧ DependsOn … giving 1 0 ∧ ¬ DependsOn … giving 2 0 ∧ Ends … (fun w => w 0) start ∧ Ends … (fun w => w 2) start. stopped: with no draw on the second, the first ends and ∀ n, (…).state n 2 = 2
laws.says: Small computed pairs and a chain of three: a partner's level saving a condition; without mutual support the order of fates breaking; an end passing down a chain past direct dependence; and a draw of nothing on the chain stopping that.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.Coupled.first_regime
laws.statement: theorem first_regime (g : Nat → Nat) (g₂ : Nat → Nat → Nat) (H₁ H₂ : Nat) (s : Nat × Nat) : ∀ n, ((Law.run (step Drawn.whole (fun a _ => g a) g₂ H₁ H₂) s).state n).1 = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step g H₁) s.1).state n
laws.says: A condition whose giving reads only what is left of itself runs as the one-condition step, whatever its partner does. This is the only tie in RegimeMargin between the coupled step and the step that LineOnAStock, WayOfUnits and TurningInTime use; those three use none of Coupled (grep).

laws.name: TurningInTime.pair, net
laws.statement: def pair (after : W → Nat → W) (left : W → Nat → Nat) (s : W × Nat) : W × Nat := (after s.1 s.2, left s.1 s.2). def net (need : Nat) (after) (left) : «际» (W × Nat) := Law.stepWhile (fun s => need ≤ s.2) (pair after left)
laws.says: A way and one level step together; the level after a step is any function `left` of the way and the level. Every law that names a giving takes left := fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x, so the way enters the level only through one number, its use; the lock's section takes left := windowLeft fB (:1276), a function of the share, the level and the rule.

laws.name: TurningInTime.rising_takes_all
laws.statement: theorem rising_takes_all {alone : W → W} {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : W → Nat} {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi) {w : W} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) (rises : ∀ j, j < hi → use (Law.orbit alone w j) < use (Law.orbit alone w (j + 1))) : (Law.orbit (asItWas alone (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) (w, x) (hi + 1)).2 = 0
laws.says: With nothing given from nothing and the step under no draw keeping every level up to hi within hi, from a level at most hi, a use that rises strictly at each of the first hi steps leaves the level at nothing at step hi + 1. The cap on the level is a premise.

laws.name: TurningInTime.turns_in_time_iff
laws.statement: Hypotheses: [DecidablePred marked]; outside : AloneOutside marked alone after; turns : ∀ w x, marked x → Kept (after w x); kept : ∀ w x, Kept w → Kept (after w x); uses : ∀ w, Kept w → use w = H₂; nothing : FromNothing giving; short : Short giving H₂ y₂; meets : Meets giving H₂ y₂ hi; keeps : Keeps giving H₂ hi; needs : 0 < need; within : need ≤ H₂ + y₂; short₁ : Short giving H₁ y₁; uses₁ : ∀ j, H₁ ≤ use (Law.orbit alone w j); below : x < H₁ + y₁; high : x ≤ hi. Conclusion: «不穷» (net need after (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) «一» (w, x) ↔ ∃ T, (∀ j, j < T → need ≤ X j ∧ ¬ marked (X j)) ∧ need ≤ X T ∧ marked (X T) ∧ H₂ + y₂ ≤ X (T + 1), X j the level at step j of the orbit of asItWas alone (same left) from (w, x)
laws.says: Under these premises the line never ends exactly where, at the first marked level of the course as it was, the need met there and before, the level one step later is at or above H₂ + y₂. Which levels are marked, the kept kind and its one use are premises.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.left, after
laws.statement: def after (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) : List U → Nat → List U | [], _ => [] | u :: w, x => cond (decide (need u ≤ x)) (kids u) [] ++ after need kids w x. def left (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) (x : Nat) : Nat := RegimeMargin.step giving (taken use w) x
laws.says: Each unit leaves its kids where the level meets its need. The level loses the total of the uses of the units present and gains giving of what is left. Units only take; the one thing added is the stock's own giving, a function of what is left of that one level.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.account
laws.statement: theorem account {s : List U × Nat} (N : Nat) (within : ∀ t, t < N → taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1 ≤ (course need kids giving use s t).2) : (course need kids giving use s N).2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1) = s.2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => giving ((course need kids giving use s t).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1))
laws.says: While what the way takes is within the level, the level at step N with everything taken before it is the start level with everything given before it. This is the line's own balance; it names no flow, web or giver.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.need_unmet
laws.statement: theorem need_unmet {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi) (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (needs : Needing need kids w) (high : x ≤ hi) (ne : w ≠ []) (met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x) : ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ hi + 1 ∧ (∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (course … (w, x) j).1 → need u ≤ (course … (w, x) j).2) ∧ (∀ j, j ≤ n → (course … (w, x) j).1 = generation kids j w) ∧ ∃ u, u ∈ (course … (w, x) n).1 ∧ (course … (w, x) n).2 < need u
laws.says: On a capped stock that gives nothing from nothing, a way every unit of which has kids that together take more than it, every need met at the start and every descendant needing something, comes to an unmet need within hi + 1 steps; until then the way is its generations, in which no giving, use or level appears.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.way_ends, line_ends
laws.statement: theorem way_ends {hi : Nat} (nothing : FromNothing giving) (keeps : Keeps giving 0 hi) (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) (needs : ∀ u, 0 < need u) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) {w} {x} (high : x ≤ hi) : (∃ n, ¬ Goes need (course need kids giving use (w, x) n)) ∧ ¬ «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (w, x). line_ends: the same for a decidable S with closed : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u and grows, needs, down asked of S only, concluding ∃ n, ∀ k, n ≤ k → ∀ u, u ∈ (course … (w, x) k).1 → ¬ S u
laws.says: On such a stock a way whose units' kids take more, with positive needs and kids needing no more than their parent, ends; a closed line with those properties inside a larger way is gone from some step on. No bound on the step in line_ends.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds
laws.statement: theorem unending_iff_holds {y : Nat → Nat} {hi : Nat} {w : List U} {x : Nat} (even : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) = use u) (some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) (needs : Needing need kids w) (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (high : x ≤ hi) (along : ∀ k, (∀ j, j ≤ k → Goes need (course … (w, x) j)) → Regime giving use y hi (course … (w, x) k).1) : «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (w, x) ↔ ∃ k, (∀ j, j < k → Goes need (course … (w, x) j)) ∧ Holds need use y (course … (w, x) k)
laws.says: Where each unit's kids take exactly what it takes, with the regime premises along the course, the net never ends exactly where the course comes to a way all of whose needs are met at a level at or above what the way takes and y of it.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.ways_alike
laws.statement: theorem ways_alike {g g' : Nat → Nat} {use use' : U → Nat} {w : List U} {x x' n : Nat} (alike : ∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids g use (w, x) j).1 → (need u ≤ (course need kids g use (w, x) j).2 ↔ need u ≤ (course need kids g' use' (w, x') j).2)) : ∀ j, j ≤ n → (course need kids g use (w, x) j).1 = (course need kids g' use' (w, x') j).1
laws.says: Two courses from one way, under any two givings, uses and start levels: while their levels meet the same needs, the ways are the same. Who is in the way depends on the level only through which needs it meets.

laws.name: WayOfUnits.more_use_on_first; With.goes_on; Against.turns_and_ends
laws.statement: theorem more_use_on_first {giving} {m n h H₂ h' H₂' y₂' hi x : Nat} (order : n ≤ m) (nothing : FromNothing giving) (short' : Short giving H₂' y₂') (meets' : Meets giving H₂' y₂' hi) (keeps' : Keeps giving H₂' hi) (sum : h + H₂ = h' + H₂') (more : h ≤ h') (high : x ≤ hi) : «不穷» (net giving) «一» ([(m, h), (n, H₂)], x) → «不穷» (net giving) «一» ([(m, h'), (n, H₂')], x). With.goes_on : «不穷» (net TurningInTime.Three.giving) «一» (way, 9) with way = [(9,4),(1,1)]. Against.turns_and_ends : … ¬ «不穷» (net TurningInTime.Three.giving) «一» (way, 9) with way = [(9,1),(1,4)]
laws.says: Two units on one level, the first needing no less: with the same sum taken, more of it on the unit that needs more never ends a line that did not end (general, its premises as listed). The two examples: same needs, same sum, same start; the line goes on where the unit that ends first took the larger share and ends where it took the smaller.

laws.name: ScratchCovering.level, gift
laws.statement: def gift (need give : U → Nat) (w : List U) (z : Nat) : Nat := total w fun u => cond (decide (need u ≤ z)) (give u) 0. def level (need : U → Nat) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use give : U → Nat) (w : List U) (x : Nat) : Nat := RegimeMargin.step giving (taken use w) x + gift need give w (x - taken use w)
laws.says: The only place in my files where units of the model add to the level: each unit whose need is met by what is left after the take adds a constant `give u`. `give` is a free function of the unit; nothing ties it to what the unit took or to anything else in the model.

laws.name: ScratchCovering.covered
laws.statement: theorem covered {need use give : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {giving : Nat → Nat} (some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) (covers : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) ≤ give u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (ne : w ≠ []) (met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x - taken use w) : (∀ n, (course … (w, x) n).1 = generation kids n w ∧ (∀ u, u ∈ (course … n).1 → need u ≤ (course … n).2 - taken use (course … n).1) ∧ (course … n).2 - taken use (course … n).1 ≤ (course … (n + 1)).2 - taken use (course … (n + 1)).1) ∧ «不穷» (net need kids giving use give) «一» (w, x)
laws.says: Scratch, not landed, not built by me. Where each unit puts back at least what all its kids together take, from a way whose needs are met by what is left, the way is its generations for ever, what is left never falls and the net never ends. For a way that grows this asks each unit to put back more than it took.

laws.name: ScratchCovering.OneKind.unending_iff
laws.statement: theorem unending_iff {a t b k N x : Nat} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : «不穷» (net (need a) (kids k) nothing (use t) (give b)) «一» (List.replicate N (), x) ↔ k * t ≤ b ∧ a + t * N ≤ x
laws.says: Scratch. One kind of unit (need a, takes t, puts back b, leaves k of itself) on a stock that gives nothing, N units at x: the net never ends exactly where b covers what the k kids take and the level covers the need after the whole first take. A law of this one family of models, for all its parameters.

laws.name: ScratchMixedWay.mixed_turns_iff
laws.statement: Hypotheses: ne : R ≠ []; self : ∀ u, u ∈ R → kids u = [u]; rn : ∀ u, u ∈ R → need u = n; take : taken use R = H₂; line : ∀ u, u ∈ c → S u; sm : ∀ u, S u → need u = m; closed : ∀ u v, S u → v ∈ kids u → S v; order : n ≤ m; keepsUse : ∀ u, S u → use u ≤ taken use (kids u); nothing; short : Short giving H₂ y₂; meets : Meets giving H₂ y₂ hi; keeps : Keeps giving H₂ hi; needs : 0 < n; within : n ≤ H₂ + y₂; short₁ : Short giving (H₂ + taken use c) y₁; below : x < H₂ + taken use c + y₁; high : x ≤ hi. Conclusion: «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (c ++ R, x) ↔ ∃ T, (∀ j, j < T → m ≤ levelAsItWas kids use giving H₂ c x j) ∧ n ≤ levelAsItWas … T ∧ levelAsItWas … T < m ∧ H₂ + y₂ ≤ levelAsItWas … (T + 1)
laws.says: Scratch. Two lines on one level with nothing put back: a line of one need m whose kids take no less, beside units of need n ≤ m that leave themselves. The whole goes on exactly where the first line's need goes unmet early enough that the level one step later still holds what the others take. The line that needs more ends; the other can go on.

laws.name: ReadOffInTime.FourReaders.balances, stopped_is_regime
laws.statement: theorem balances : ∀ k, (flow k).Balances (web k). theorem stopped_is_regime : ∀ k n, habitat k (n + stopAt k) = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step giving 1) (habitat k (stopAt k))).state n, with giving z = if 1 ≤ z then 1 else 0 (:1025), and in flow (:849) take .dweller .habitat = if 1 ≤ habitat k t then 1 else 0, give .renewer .habitat = if 2 ≤ habitat k t then 1 else 0, take .renewer _ = 0, requires .renewer _ = False
laws.says: Four tabulated courses over three conditions with eight formations. Each balances as a flow on its web, and once the clearer stops the habitat's level is the run of RegimeMargin's step under a draw of one. The draw is the dweller's take and the giving is the give of a formation that takes and requires nothing. Not on my list; it is the only place in the package where RegimeMargin's step and Flow.Balances meet.

laws.name: Flow.Balances
laws.statement: def Balances (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t c, W.level (t + 1) c + L.taken t c = W.level t c + L.given t c, with taken t c = total (L.present t) fun f => L.take t f c and given t c = total (L.present t) fun f => L.give t f c (:268, :273)
laws.says: Each condition's level after a step, with what the formations present took from it, is its level before with what they gave it. It constrains each condition, not each formation: a formation may give without taking.

laws.name: Amounts.replenishment_unbounded
laws.statement: theorem replenishment_unbounded (archimedean : M.Archimedean) {s u r : Nat → A} {ε : A} {T₀ : Nat} (positive : ¬ M.le ε M.zero) (balances : ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → M.le (M.add (s (t + 1)) (u t)) (M.add (s t) (r t))) (more : ∀ m, ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → M.le (M.times m ε) (u t)) (b : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → M.le (r t) (M.times b ε)
laws.says: For any stock, uptake and replenishment read as three sequences, balanced from some step on: where the uptake comes to exceed every multiple of a least amount, no bound holds of the replenishment. It asks for no web and no count of takers; Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded (Flow.lean:748) is its case where takers are counted.

laws.name: RuleShaping.shaped, favours_iff, favours_alike, nothing_back_falls, grouped_rises_iff

laws.statement: structure Law where start : Nat; renew : Nat; needG : Nat; needF : Nat; draw : Nat → Nat; contrib : Nat → Nat.  level L 0 = L.start;  level L (t + 1) = if L.needG ≤ level L t then (if L.needF ≤ level L t then level L t + L.renew + L.contrib t - L.draw t else level L t + L.renew) else (if L.needF ≤ level L t then level L t + L.contrib t - L.draw t else level L t)

laws.name: Law.unfolding, Law.need, Law.requiresPart, Law.drawsPart
laws.statement: need L : Part → Nat | .focal => L.needF | .sustaining => L.needG;  requiresPart L | .focal => 0 < L.needF | .sustaining => True;  drawsPart L | .focal => ∃ t, 0 < L.draw t | .sustaining => False;  unfolding L : Unfolding Part Unit where level t _ := L.level t; active t p := L.need p ≤ L.level t; requires p _ := L.requiresPart p; need p _ := L.need p; draws p _ := L.drawsPart p
laws.says: The sustaining part always requires the one condition at needG, is active exactly while the level is at or above needG, and draws on nothing. So the renewer rests on what it renews, through a threshold only: it takes nothing, and `renew` has no source. With needG = 0 the gate is always open. The focal part rests on the condition only if needF > 0.

laws.name: Law.within_renewal_renewing
laws.statement: (L : Law) (within : ∀ t, L.draw t ≤ L.renew + L.contrib t) (gStart : L.needG ≤ L.start) (fStart : L.needF ≤ L.start) : RenewingIn L.unfolding .focal ∧ (∀ t, L.unfolding.active t .focal) ∧ ∀ t, L.formed t = t
laws.says: For every law of the family: if at every step the draw is within renewal plus contribution and both parts start supported, the focal part is active at every step and both needs are kept for ever. A sufficient condition on the whole schedule, not on a state reached. `formed t = t` counts active steps.

laws.name: Law.no_return_below_support
laws.statement: (L : Law) {T : Nat} (noRestore : ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.contrib t ≤ L.draw t) (below : L.level T < L.needG) : ∀ d, L.level (T + d) ≤ L.level T
laws.says: Once the level is below the renewer's need, and from then on the focal part gives back no more than it draws, the level never rises again.

laws.name: Law.overdraw_crosses_support and Law.overdraw_consuming
laws.statement: overdraw_consuming (L : Law) (positive : 0 < L.needG) (fWithin : L.needF ≤ L.needG) {T0 : Nat} (over : ∀ t, T0 ≤ t → L.renew + L.contrib t < L.draw t) : ConsumingIn L.unfolding .focal ∧ ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → ¬ L.unfolding.active t .sustaining.  overdraw_crosses_support has the same premises and concludes ∃ T, T0 ≤ T ∧ T ≤ T0 + L.level T0 ∧ L.level T < L.needG
laws.says: If from some step on every draw exceeds renewal plus contribution, the level falls below the renewer's need within as many steps as the level then, and the renewer is inactive for ever.

laws.name: Law.dependent_overdraw_ends_itself
laws.statement: (L : Law) (fPositive : 0 < L.needF) (fWithin : L.needF ≤ L.needG) {T0 : Nat} (over : ∀ t, T0 ≤ t → L.renew + L.contrib t < L.draw t) : ∃ T, (∀ t, T ≤ t → ¬ L.unfolding.active t .focal) ∧ ∀ t, L.formed t ≤ T
laws.says: A focal part that requires the condition and overdraws it at every step from some step on ends itself.

laws.name: Law.independent_overdraw_persists
laws.statement: (L : Law) (independent : L.needF = 0) (positive : 0 < L.needG) {T0 : Nat} (over : ∀ t, T0 ≤ t → L.renew + L.contrib t < L.draw t) : (∀ t, L.unfolding.active t .focal) ∧ (∀ t, L.formed t = t) ∧ ConsumingIn L.unfolding .focal
laws.says: A focal part that does not require the condition overdraws it, stays active at every step, and the renewer is lost.

laws.name: unrenewed_drawdown_finite
laws.statement: (U : Unfolding F C) (f : F) (c : C) (T0 : Nat) (unrenewed : ∀ t, T0 ≤ t → U.level (t + 1) c ≤ U.level t c) (lowers : ∀ t, T0 ≤ t → U.active t f → U.level (t + 1) c < U.level t c) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ U.active t f
laws.says: For any unfolding: where a condition never rises and each active step of a formation lowers it, the formation is not active at arbitrarily late steps.

laws.name: Law.jointly_consuming
laws.statement: (start renew need : Nat) (d1 d2 : Nat → Nat) (within1 : ∀ t, d1 t ≤ renew) (within2 : ∀ t, d2 t ≤ renew) (joint : ∀ t, renew < d1 t + d2 t) (positive : 0 < need) (supported : need ≤ start) : RenewingIn (alone start renew need d1).unfolding .focal ∧ RenewingIn (alone start renew need d2).unfolding .focal ∧ ConsumingIn (together start renew need d1 d2).unfolding .focal ∧ ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → ¬ (together ...).unfolding.active t .focal ∧ ¬ (together ...).unfolding.active t .sustaining
laws.says: Two draw schedules each within renewal, summed beyond it: each alone renews, the two together (one law with the summed draw) consume and both parts end. Three separate laws compared, not two takers inside one web.

laws.name: Law.own_trajectory_does_not_decide (sharing, winning)
laws.statement: (∀ t, sharing.unfolding.active t .focal ↔ winning.unfolding.active t .focal) ∧ (∀ t, sharing.formed t = winning.formed t) ∧ RenewingIn sharing.unfolding .focal ∧ ConsumingIn winning.unfolding .focal, with sharing := ⟨3, 1, 1, 0, fun _ => 1, fun _ => 0⟩ and winning := ⟨3, 1, 1, 0, fun _ => 2, fun _ => 0⟩
laws.says: Two laws whose focal part is active and forms alike at every step; one renews and one consumes. The focal part does not require the condition in either.

laws.name: Law.formation_does_not_decide (cultivation, malignant) and Law.escalation_consumes
laws.statement: cultivation := ⟨2, 1, 1, 1, fun _ => 2, fun _ => 1⟩ is RenewingIn with formed t = t; malignant := ⟨4, 1, 2, 1, fun _ => 3, fun _ => 0⟩ is ConsumingIn and ∃ T with the focal part inactive from T and formed t ≤ T. escalation := ⟨3, 2, 1, 1, fun t => t, fun _ => 0⟩: (∀ t, t ≤ 2 → draw t ≤ renew + contrib t) ∧ level 3 = 6 ∧ formed 3 = 3 ∧ ConsumingIn ∧ ∃ T, focal inactive from T ∧ ∀ t, formed t ≤ T
laws.says: Cultivation draws 2 and gives back 1 with renewal 1; its level is constant 2. Escalation's draw is the step number, set from outside: it is within renewal for three steps and then ends.

laws.name: SupportGated.renewal, netGive, flow
laws.statement: renewal L t := if L.needG ≤ L.level t then L.renew else 0;  netGive L t := if L.needF ≤ L.level t then L.contrib t - L.draw t else 0;  flow : Flow Part Unit where present _ := [.sustaining, .focal]; give t p _ := match p with | .sustaining => renewal L t | .focal => netGive L t; take t p _ := match p with | .sustaining => 0 | .focal => L.level t + (renewal L t + netGive L t) - L.level (t + 1)
laws.says: The Law read as a flow. The sustaining part gives the renewal while supported and takes nothing. The focal part gives only what it contributes beyond its draw, and its take is defined as whatever the step removes.

laws.name: SupportGated.balances and SupportGated.givers_supported
laws.statement: theorem balances : (flow L).Balances (web L);  theorem givers_supported (t : Nat) : (flow L).GiversSupported (web L) t ()
laws.says: For every law of the family the flow above balances its static web, by construction of the focal take; and whatever gives a positive amount is supported at that step.

laws.name: SupportGated.repair_restores
laws.statement: (T : Nat) (fOn : L.needF ≤ L.level T) (exceeds : ∀ d, d < L.needG - L.level T → L.draw (T + d) < L.contrib (T + d)) : L.needG ≤ L.level (T + (L.needG - L.level T))
laws.says: Where the focal part is active and contributes more than it draws at each of needG − level steps, the level is back at the renewer's need. An instance of Flow.restores.

laws.name: SupportGated.below_for_good and ends_for_good
laws.statement: below_for_good {T : Nat} (noRestore : ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.contrib t ≤ L.draw t) {bound : Nat} (below : L.level T < bound) (within : bound ≤ L.needG) : ∀ n, L.level (T + n) < bound.  ends_for_good adds (p : Part) (depends : L.requiresPart p) (high : bound ≤ L.need p) (n : Nat) and concludes ¬ L.unfolding.active (T + n) p
laws.says: The Law's loss for good, as instances of Flow.stays_below_at and Flow.ends_below_at.

laws.name: SupportRecovery.absorbs
laws.statement: (L : Law) (T : Nat) (fOff : L.level T < L.needF) (gOff : L.level T < L.needG) : ∀ n, L.level (T + n) = L.level T
laws.says: Where both parts have lost their support the level never moves again, whatever the schedules say.

laws.name: SupportRecovery.pulse with pulse_levels, supported_pulse_recovers, unsupported_pulse_ends, recovered_neither
laws.statement: pulse firstDraw := ⟨2, 1, 2, 1, (fun | 0 => firstDraw | _ + 1 => 0), (fun | 0 => 0 | _ + 1 => 1)⟩.  pulse_levels: levels of pulse 2 are 2, 1, 2 and of pulse 3 are 2, 0.  supported_pulse_recovers (n : Nat) : 2 ≤ (pulse 2).level (2 + n).  unsupported_pulse_ends (n) : level (1 + n) () = 0 ∧ ∀ p, ¬ active (1 + n) p.  recovered_neither : ¬ RenewingIn (pulse 2).unfolding .focal ∧ ¬ ConsumingIn (pulse 2).unfolding .focal
laws.says: Two histories differing in the first draw only. In one the focal part's later contribution lifts the level back to the renewer's need and renewal resumes; in the other everything stops at zero. The recovered history is neither renewing nor consuming: the two sufficient conditions leave a gap.

laws.name: Flow.Balances
laws.statement: def Balances (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t c, W.level (t + 1) c + L.taken t c = W.level t c + L.given t c, with taken t c := total (L.present t) fun f => L.take t f c and given t c := total (L.present t) fun f => L.give t f c
laws.says: Each change of a level is what the listed formations give minus what they take. It does not ask that what is given be taken from anywhere, and it has no order of taking and giving inside a step.

laws.name: Flow.stays_below_at and Flow.stays_below
laws.statement: stays_below (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {c : C} {m : Nat} (gated : ∀ t f, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.give t f c → W.requires t f c ∧ m ≤ W.need t f c) {T : Nat} (below : W.level T c < m) : ∀ n, W.level (T + n) c < m
laws.says: For every balanced flow: where everything that gives to a condition requires that condition at a need of at least m, only active formations give and activity needs support, a level once below m stays below m. Renewal that depends on what it renews does not come back.

laws.name: Flow.joint_excess_ends
laws.statement: (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) (dependent : W.Dependent) {c : C} {m : Nat} (gated : ∀ t f, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.give t f c → W.requires t f c ∧ m ≤ W.need t f c) {T n : Nat} (excess : ∀ k, k < n → L.given (T + k) c < L.taken (T + k) c) (start : W.level T c < n + m) : ∀ k g, W.requires (T + n + k) g c → m ≤ W.need (T + n + k) g c → ¬ W.active (T + n + k) g
laws.says: Under the same gate, n steps of taking more than is given from a level below n + m leave every formation that requires the condition at a need of at least m inactive from then on, the takers included.

laws.name: Flow.joint_keeps and Flow.restores
laws.statement: joint_keeps (balances : L.Balances W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (within : L.WithinJoint t c) : W.level t c ≤ W.level (t + 1) c, where WithinJoint L t c := L.taken t c ≤ L.given t c.  restores (balances : L.Balances W) {c : C} {m T : Nat} (netGive : ∀ k, k < m - W.level T c → W.level T c ≤ W.level (T + k) c → L.taken (T + k) c < L.given (T + k) c) : m ≤ W.level (T + (m - W.level T c)) c
laws.says: Taking jointly within what is given, the level does not fall. Giving jointly more than is taken at each of m − level steps brings the level to m.

laws.name: Flow.fed_from_beyond and Flow.Dissipative.finite_taking_not_recurring
laws.statement: fed_from_beyond [DecidableEq C] (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {ds : List C} (distinct : Distinct ds) {T₀ : Nat} (around : ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.Around ds t) (recurs : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers ds t) (N : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, N ≤ t → ¬ L.FedFromBeyond ds t.  finite_taking_not_recurring (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {all : List C} (distinct : Distinct all) (every : ∀ c, c ∈ all) (cs : List C) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers cs t.  DissipatesOn cs t := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → total cs (L.give t f) + sign (total cs (L.take t f)) ≤ total cs (L.take t f)
laws.says: Where every formation gives a closed family no more than it takes from it, and less when it takes: a finite family that keeps being taken from cannot stop being fed from a condition outside it, and if finitely many conditions are all there is, taking does not go on. Proofs not read, statements only.

laws.name: Web.Unceasing.rises and Web.Unceasing.activeRenewer_recurs
laws.statement: rises {cs : List C} (depletes : W.Depletes cs fun t => ∃ f, W.Arises t f) (unceasing : W.Unceasing) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.Still cs t.  activeRenewer_recurs {renews : Nat → F → C → Prop} {cs : List C} (made : W.RenewedBy renews) (depletes : ...) (unceasing : W.Unceasing) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → ∀ f, ¬ W.ActiveRenewer renews cs t f
laws.says: On any web, with no flow: where each arising lowers some condition of a finite family at steps at which none rises, arising without end needs some condition of the family to rise at arbitrarily late steps; and where each rise is made by an active formation, under a `renews` relation that the user supplies, renewing activity recurs. A necessary condition only.

laws.name: Web.substitution_defers and Web.dissipation_arising_not_recurring
laws.statement: substitution_defers (cs : List C) (f : F) (T : Nat) (still : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.Still cs t) (draws_down : W.Depletes cs fun t => W.active t f) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ W.active t f.  dissipation_arising_not_recurring (q : Nat → Nat) (unrestored : ∀ t, q (t + 1) ≤ q t) (dissipates : ∀ t f, W.Arises t f → q (t + 1) < q t) : ¬ W.Unceasing
laws.says: A formation that lowers some condition of a finite family at each active step, while none rises, is not active at arbitrarily late steps however it moves among them. If a quantity never rises and every arising lowers it, arising ceases.

laws.name: Recycle.closed_unceasing
laws.statement: web.Dependent ∧ web.RenewedBy renews ∧ web.Depletes [.a, .b] (fun t => ∃ f, web.Arises t f) ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ (∀ t, web.stock [.a, .b] t = 1) ∧ ∀ T, ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → ∀ f, ¬ web.ActiveRenewer renews [.a, .b] t f
laws.says: One unit passing between two pools. The consumer requires pool a and is active at even steps; a carrier, always active and requiring nothing, is said to renew a, and the consumer's drawing is said to renew b, by a relation written by hand. The total stays one and the consumer arises at every odd step. No Flow is defined for it anywhere in the package, and `Depletes` holds vacuously (the consumer arises only where a rises).

laws.name: Oscillation.unceasing, Oscillation.readings, Oscillation.not_more
laws.statement: unceasing : web.Dependent ∧ web.RenewedBy renews ∧ web.Depletes [()] (fun t => ∃ f, web.Arises t f) ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ∀ T, ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → ∀ f, ¬ web.ActiveRenewer renews [()] t f.  readings : (∀ n, web.UnderminingAt (2 * n) .oscillator) ∧ web.RenewingInWithin 2 .oscillator.  not_more : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ¬ flow.More [()]
laws.says: One condition at 2, 1, 2, 1, … A source, always active and requiring nothing, gives one at every step and takes nothing; an oscillator needing two takes two when active and arises at every odd step. The renewer stands outside; there is no loop. Each arising undermines by the stepwise reading and renews over cycles of two.

laws.name: Relay.defers
laws.statement: web.Dependent ∧ web.active 0 () ∧ web.active 1 () ∧ web.Dissolves 0 () .first ∧ web.Forms 0 () .second ∧ web.ConsumingIn () ∧ (∀ t, 2 ≤ t → ¬ web.active t ()) ∧ ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ web.active t ()
laws.says: One consumer and two sources of one unit each, neither renewed: it moves its dependence from the first to the second and is inactive from step 2. No flow.

laws.name: Growth.ceases
laws.statement: web.Dependent ∧ web.Arises 0 0 ∧ web.Arises 1 1 ∧ web.ConsumingIn 0 ∧ (∀ t, ¬ web.Rises t ()) ∧ ¬ web.Unceasing, with level t _ := left t (3, 2, 1, then 0) and active t n := n < t ∧ 1 ≤ left t
laws.says: Cells indexed by number arise (two of them) on a condition of three units that nothing renews; it is consumed and arising stops. The level is a declared sequence falling by one a step whatever the number of active cells (it falls at step 0 with none active); no flow.

laws.name: Tide.unrelated_depletion and Tide.renewal_without_arising
laws.statement: renewal_without_arising : still.RenewedBy renews ∧ (∀ T, ∃ t, T ≤ t ∧ still.Rises t ()) ∧ (∀ T, ∃ t f, T ≤ t ∧ still.ActiveRenewer renews [()] t f) ∧ ∀ t f, ¬ still.Arises t f
laws.says: A level going 0, 1, 0, 1 with a moon, always active and requiring nothing, said to renew it. Renewal recurs with nothing arising; and a flicker that neither requires nor draws on the tide counts as depleting it.

laws.name: Flow.Cycle.closed_more
laws.statement: flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Dependent ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ (∀ t, web.stock [()] (t + 1) = web.stock [()] t) ∧ ∀ t, flow.renewers [()] t = flow.takers [()] t, with flow := ⟨present, fun _ _ _ => 1, fun _ _ _ => 1⟩ and web: level _ _ := 1, active t n := n < t, requires t n _ := n < t, need 1, draws t n _ := n < t
laws.says: Formation n arises at step n and stays, so the number present grows without end; each requires the one condition at need one, takes one and gives one back. The level stays at 1. The only place I read where the formations that give multiply; their number is set by the index, and nothing is selected.

laws.name: Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded
laws.statement: {cs : List C} (balances : L.Balances W) (more : L.More cs) (R T₀ : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.replenishment cs t ≤ R, with More cs := ∀ K, ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → K ≤ L.takers cs t and takers counting listed formations with a positive take
laws.says: In a balanced flow, where the number of formations taking from a finite family grows past every number, no bound holds on what is given to the family. What is given may be the takers' own giving back (Cycle).

laws.name: falls_not_recurring
laws.statement: (rank : Nat → Nat) (T : Nat) (noRise : ∀ n, T ≤ n → rank (n + 1) ≤ rank n) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ rank (n + 1) < rank n
laws.says: A whole-number quantity that never rises from some step on does not fall at arbitrarily late steps. The one theorem of Renewal.lean, and the descent used by Arising, Reserve and Flow.

laws.name: RenewalBound.no_renewal_free_tail and renewal_arbitrarily_late
laws.statement: no_renewal_free_tail {unrenewed : State → State → Prop} (wellFounded : WellFounded unrenewed) (states : Nat → State) (renewal : Nat → Prop) (decreases : ∀ n, ¬ renewal n → unrenewed (states (n + 1)) (states n)) (start : Nat) : ¬ (∀ n, start ≤ n → ¬ renewal n)
laws.says: Where every step that is not a renewal descends a well-founded relation, no tail of an unending sequence is free of renewal. It says renewal must recur if the sequence goes on; it does not say who renews. The alternation (:173-245) is its built example.

laws.name: Web.Carries.active_not_recurring and Flow.carries_of_held
laws.statement: active_not_recurring (carries : W.Carries r) {f : F} {T : Nat} (unsupported : ∀ t, T ≤ t → ¬ W.Supported t f) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ W.active t f.  carries_of_held (balances : L.Balances W) (hold : F → C) (unreplenished : ∀ t f, ¬ W.Supported t f → L.given t (hold f) = 0) (drawn : ∀ t f, ¬ W.Supported t f → W.active t f → 0 < L.taken t (hold f)) : W.Carries fun t f => W.level t (hold f)
laws.says: A reserve that does not rise while its formation is unsupported and falls at each unsupported active step defers the end and does not escape it. In a balanced flow a held condition that nothing gives to and that is taken from at such steps is such a reserve.

laws.name: Web.consumed_iff and Slowing.slowing_recovery
laws.statement: consumed_iff {c : C} : W.Consumed c ↔ ∃ g T, W.requires T g c ∧ ¬ ∃ k, 0 < k ∧ W.need T g c ≤ W.level (T + k) c.  slowing_recovery : web.Restored () ∧ ¬ web.Consumed () ∧ ∀ p, ¬ web.RenewedWithin p ()
laws.says: Being consumed is exactly some dependence never met again (a rewording of the definition; general). The built example Slowing has a condition met again after ever longer gaps: it always returns and no cycle length bounds the return.

laws.name: Web.consumed_ends_when_fixed and Web.consumed_continues_transformed
laws.statement: consumed_ends_when_fixed (dependent : W.Dependent) {T : Nat} {g : F} {c : C} (fixed : ∀ t, T < t → W.requires t g c ∧ W.need T g c ≤ W.need t g c) (below : ∀ t, T < t → W.level t c < W.need T g c) : ∀ t, T < t → ¬ W.active t g.  consumed_continues_transformed (dependent) (below) {t} (later : T < t) (active : W.active t g) : ¬ (W.requires t g c ∧ W.need T g c ≤ W.need t g c)
laws.says: Where activity needs support: after a loss without return, a formation whose dependence is unchanged is no longer active, and one still active has weakened or dropped the dependence. Both are contrapositives of `Dependent`.

laws.name: Unmet.consumed_without_loss
laws.statement: web.Dependent ∧ (∀ t g, ¬ web.Broken t g ()) ∧ web.Consumed () ∧ ¬ web.Lost () ∧ web.ConsumingIn .drawer ∧ ∀ t, ¬ web.UnderminingAt t .drawer
laws.says: A web in which no level ever changes: a requirement never met makes its condition 'consumed' and whoever is marked as drawing on it 'consuming'. The class turns on who is marked as drawing, not on amounts.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds (November, for comparison)
laws.statement: {y : Nat → Nat} {hi : Nat} {w : List U} {x : Nat} (even : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) = use u) (some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) (needs : Needing need kids w) (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (high : x ≤ hi) (along : ∀ k, (∀ j, j ≤ k → Goes need (course need kids giving use (w, x) j)) → Regime giving use y hi (course need kids giving use (w, x) k).1) : «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (w, x) ↔ ∃ k, (∀ j, j < k → Goes need (course need kids giving use (w, x) j)) ∧ Holds need use y (course need kids giving use (w, x) k)
laws.says: An exact condition on a state reached: under the seven premises the course never ends exactly where it comes to a configuration with every need met and the level at or above what the way takes plus y of it. Units leave kids; by `even` the kids together take what the parent took, so multiplying does not raise the draw in this statement. The level gives `giving` of what is left after the take; no formation gives.

laws.name: FourReaders.balances and FourReaders.stopped_is_regime
laws.statement: balances : ∀ k, (flow k).Balances (web k).  stopped_is_regime : ∀ k n, habitat k (n + stopAt k) = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step giving 1) (habitat k (stopAt k))).state n, with giving z := if 1 ≤ z then 1 else 0 and the flow's renewer giving `if 2 ≤ habitat k t then 1 else 0`
laws.says: A web with fixed numbers on which a flow balances and whose habitat level, once the clearer stops, is the run of RegimeMargin's step under a draw of one. The renewer requires nothing in the web.

laws.name: Flow.Growing.growing and Repeated.more_without_arising
laws.statement: growing : flow.Balances web ∧ (∀ t, web.Rises t ()) ∧ (∀ t, ¬ web.ComesToStand t ()) ∧ ∀ t, 0 < flow.given t (), with flow := Witnesses.giving () 1 and level t + 1.  more_without_arising : web.Census (fun _ => [()]) ∧ flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ ¬ (∀ t, Distinct (flow.present t)) ∧ ∀ t f, ¬ web.Arises t f
laws.says: A balanced web on which one formation gives one unit at every step for ever and the level grows without bound, nothing taken. And a balanced flow that lists one formation t times at step t, each entry taking one and giving one back.

PKG and DEEPER are as defined under read_in_part. All of this is from reading; nothing was built.

WHAT THE SUPPORT-GATED RENEWAL LAW IS. One level and six inputs (start, renew, needG, needF, a draw schedule, a contribution schedule). The sustaining part adds the fixed amount `renew` at each step where the level is at or above its own need needG, and the web says it always requires that condition. So the renewer rests on what it renews, and that is the loop. But the loop is a threshold and nothing else: the sustaining part takes nothing (`drawsPart .sustaining => False`; take 0 in the flow), `renew` has no source, and the level it rests on is not used up by its resting. The focal part draws and may contribute while the level is at or above needF; with needF = 0 it stands outside. Draw and contribution are schedules handed in; nothing in the model makes them depend on the level, on a count, or on each other.

IS THERE AN 'EXACTLY WHERE' LAW FOR A RENEWED CONDITION WITH TAKERS. Not in the eight files. The family has a sufficient condition for going on for ever (`within_renewal_renewing`: every step's draw within renewal plus contribution) and sufficient conditions for ending (`overdraw_consuming`, `dependent_overdraw_ends_itself`: every step from some step on beyond it), both over the whole schedule, and the gap between them is proved inhabited (`SupportRecovery.recovered_neither`, `fluctuating_neither`). The one-way law nearest a point of no return is `no_return_below_support` and its form for every flow, `Flow.stays_below`: once below the renewer's need, always below. The package's 'iff' laws about unceasing arising that I looked at (`Change.unceasing_iff`, `Population.unceasing_iff_bounded`) say arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs; they are about counts of active formations, not amounts. Against `LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds`: that one is exact and is about a state the course reaches; its giving is a function of the level left after the take and belongs to no formation; its units leave kids. October's has a renewer that is a formation resting on the level, a gate read before the step, renewal added before the draw is subtracted, and no units. The two steps agree wherever the level is at least the draw and differ where the draw exceeds it (hand transcription in /Users/ren/theories/tmp/r7/one-model/check/round16/search/renewal/check_law.py, item 4; not Lean). No theorem in what I read joins `RelationalRenewal.Law` to `RegimeMargin.step`; RegimeMargin has `Gated g m` (RegimeMargin.lean:268), which is the same idea of giving that stops below a need.

WHERE THE FROZEN FILE'S PICTURE IS DRAWN WRONG.
1. 'October's Lean does not allow an amount that grows by a rule of its own.' It does. A `Web` is five free functions (World.lean:48-57); its levels can be any sequences, and `Recycle`, `Growth`, `Relay` and `Tide` are stated on declared levels with no flow at all. `Flow.Balances` is a further premise used in some modules, and it only attributes each rise to a listed giver; `Growing.growing` is a balanced web growing by one a step for ever. The sentence 'a sun or a river is then one of the formations, not an outside' is from the opening account of Arising.lean (lines 21-25) and is conditional there ('when the unfolding has no source of renewal outside its formations'); the Lean behind it is the definition `RenewedBy`, a premise a user may or may not supply, with `renews` left to the application. What does forbid giving from nothing is `Flow.Dissipative` (Dissipation.lean:248), and six of Flow.lean's witnesses, Cycle and Oscillation among them, are proved not dissipative (`witnesses_not_dissipative`, Dissipation.lean:1369). By my reading of the definition `SupportGated.flow` is not dissipative either wherever renewal is positive; no theorem states that.
2. So October has three layers, not one: the web alone, balance (who gave), and balance with dissipation. Under the third, with finitely many conditions, nothing that takes goes on at all (`Dissipative.finite_taking_not_recurring`), and a family that keeps being taken from is fed from outside it (`Flow.fed_from_beyond`). Every October example of going on for ever that I read sits in the first or second layer.
3. In the support-gated family nothing multiplies and multiplying costs nothing: `formed` counts active steps and never enters the level. The closest thing to growing takers is `escalation`, whose draw is the step number, set from outside. In `Flow.Cycle` the formations do multiply and each gives back what it takes, so the level never moves. In `LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds` the premise `even` likewise makes the kids take what the parent took. In neither month's statement that I read does multiplying by itself raise the draw on what is rested on.

Recovery and staying below do (`Flow.restores`, `Flow.stays_below_at`, `Flow.ends_below_at`). The crossing does not: `overdraw_ends` and `jointly_ends` call `Law.overdraw_crosses_support`, proved by its own induction in DEEPER/RelationalRenewal.lean.
