laws.name: Flow.Balances
laws.statement: def Balances (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t c, W.level (t + 1) c + L.taken t c = W.level t c + L.given t c
laws.says: Each level after a step, with what the formations present took from it, equals the level before with what they gave to it. There is no order inside a step and nothing is asked of who gives; with nothing taken and nothing given the level stays.

laws.name: Flow.takers / Flow.renewers / Flow.More
laws.statement: def takers (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Nat := count (L.present t) fun f => total cs (L.take t f); def renewers ... := count (L.present t) fun f => total cs (L.give t f); def More (cs : List C) : Prop := ∀ K, ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → K ≤ L.takers cs t
laws.says: Takers and renewers count formations with a positive gross take or give. A unit that takes h and gives h back is one taker and one renewer; its net form is neither.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.rise_given / Flow.Balances.fall_taken
laws.statement: theorem Balances.rise_given (balances : L.Balances W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (rises : W.Rises t c) : 0 < L.given t c; theorem Balances.fall_taken (balances : L.Balances W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (falls : W.Falls t c) : 0 < L.taken t c
laws.says: Under balance a level that rises was given to and a level that falls was taken from. This is all balance says of change; it says an untouched level stays, not that it cannot.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.replenished_over
laws.statement: theorem Balances.replenished_over {cs : List C} {K S : Nat} (balances : L.Balances W) (many : ∀ t, S ≤ t → K ≤ L.takers cs t) (N : Nat) : K * N ≤ W.stock cs S + total (steps S N) (L.replenishment cs)
laws.says: Under balance, if at least K formations take from the family at every step from S, then over N steps K times N is at most the stock at S plus everything given to the family, by anyone, the takers included.

laws.name: Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded
laws.statement: theorem More.replenishment_unbounded {cs : List C} (balances : L.Balances W) (more : L.More cs) (R T₀ : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.replenishment cs t ≤ R
laws.says: Under balance and more takers without end, no bound from any step on bounds what is given to the family. It does not say the giving comes from outside the takers.

laws.name: Flow.Cycle.closed_more
laws.statement: theorem closed_more : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Dependent ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ (∀ t, web.stock [()] (t + 1) = web.stock [()] t) ∧ ∀ t, flow.renewers [()] t = flow.takers [()] t   (flow := ⟨present, fun _ _ _ => 1, fun _ _ _ => 1⟩, web.level _ _ := 1)
laws.says: On one condition standing at 1, t formations each take 1 and give 1 back at step t: balanced, more without end, stock constant, as many renewers as takers. All t are supported by the one level 1, since requirement is a threshold.

laws.name: Flow.Growing.growing
laws.statement: theorem growing : flow.Balances web ∧ (∀ t, web.Rises t ()) ∧ (∀ t, ¬ web.ComesToStand t ()) ∧ ∀ t, 0 < flow.given t ()   (flow := Witnesses.giving () 1, web := Witnesses.unrequired (fun t _ => t + 1) (fun _ _ => True))
laws.says: One formation that takes nothing and requires nothing gives 1 at every step and the level rises for ever, balanced. A giver from nowhere is allowed by balance.

laws.name: Web.Supported
laws.statement: def Supported (t : Nat) (f : F) : Prop := ∀ c, W.requires t f c → W.need t f c ≤ W.level t c
laws.says: A formation is supported where every condition it requires stands at or above its need. Requiring is a threshold on the level; it takes nothing.

laws.name: Flow.DissipatesOn / Flow.Dissipative
laws.statement: def DissipatesOn (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Prop := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → total cs (L.give t f) + sign (total cs (L.take t f)) ≤ total cs (L.take t f); def Dissipative : Prop := ∀ cs t, Distinct cs → L.ClosedAt cs t → L.DissipatesOn cs t
laws.says: Every formation gives a closed family no more than it takes from it, and less when it takes. This, not balance, is what rules out a pure giver and a unit giving back all it takes.

laws.name: Flow.Dissipative.opens
laws.statement: theorem Dissipative.opens (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {cs ds : List C} (distinct : Distinct ds) (within : ∀ c, c ∈ cs → c ∈ ds) (recurs : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers cs t) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.ClosedAt ds t
laws.says: Under balance and dissipation, a family taken from at arbitrarily late steps lies in no finite family that stays closed from some step on: something outside it keeps taking part. Statement read; proof not read.

laws.name: Flow.unfed_consumption_ends_at
laws.statement: theorem unfed_consumption_ends_at {c : C} {g : F} {T : Nat} (unfed : ∀ t f, T ≤ t → W.active t g → f ∈ L.present t → W.Supported t f → L.give t f c = 0) (consumes : ∀ t, T ≤ t → W.active t g → g ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.take t g c) : ∀ n, (∀ k, k < n → L.BalancesOn W [c] (T + k)) → (∀ k, k < n → L.GiversSupported W (T + k) c) → (∀ k, k < n → W.active (T + k) g) → n ≤ W.level T c
laws.says: A formation that takes from a condition at every step it is active, with nothing supported giving to that condition meanwhile, is active for at most as many consecutive steps as the level at the start. The premise is taking, not requiring. Statement read; proof not read.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.step
laws.statement: def step (g : Nat → Nat) (H x : Nat) : Nat := (x - H) + g (x - H)
laws.says: The draw takes first, as much as there is (cut-off subtraction), and the level then gives g of what is left. The giving reads the level after the take and has no named giver.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.after / left / Goes
laws.statement: def after (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) : List U → Nat → List U | [], _ => [] | u :: w, x => cond (decide (need u ≤ x)) (kids u) [] ++ after need kids w x; def left (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) (x : Nat) : Nat := RegimeMargin.step giving (taken use w) x; def Goes (need : U → Nat) (s : List U × Nat) : Prop := ∃ u, u ∈ s.1 ∧ need u ≤ s.2
laws.says: A unit leaves its kids where the level at the start of the step meets its need; the level after is the step under the total of all uses. Need is a threshold on the one level; use is what is taken; the two are separate fields.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.account
laws.statement: theorem account {s : List U × Nat} (N : Nat) (within : ∀ t, t < N → taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1 ≤ (course need kids giving use s t).2) : (course need kids giving use s N).2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1) = s.2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => giving ((course need kids giving use s t).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1))
laws.says: While what the way takes is within the level at every step before N, the level at N with everything taken equals the start level with everything given. The line's own balance; it needs `within` because the step's subtraction is cut off.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.taken_below
laws.statement: theorem taken_below (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) {s : List U × Nat} (needs : Needing need kids s.1) {n : Nat} (goes : Goes need (course need kids giving use s (n + 1))) : taken use (course need kids giving use s n).1 < (course need kids giving use s n).2
laws.says: With nothing given from nothing and every unit of every generation needing something, where some need is still met at step n+1 the way took less than the level at step n.

laws.name: RuleShaping.favours_iff
laws.statement: theorem favours_iff {a s p c : Nat} {pos : 0 < a} : CarrierCounts.favours (shaped a s p c pos) ↔ c ≤ s   (shaped a s p c pos := ⟨a + s + p, a + c + p, _⟩; favours g := g.other ≤ g.carrier)
laws.says: Where each shaper leaves a+s+p offspring and each other a+c+p, the shapers leave at least as many exactly where c ≤ s. The counts are given numbers; no level, flow or web appears, and p reaches every member whether or not any shaper is present.

laws.name: RuleShaping.favours_alike
laws.statement: theorem favours_alike {a s p p' c : Nat} {pos : 0 < a} : CarrierCounts.favours (shaped a s p c pos) ↔ CarrierCounts.favours (shaped a s p' c pos)
laws.says: Changing the part every member receives alike does not change whether the rule favours the shapers.

laws.name: RuleShaping.nothing_back_falls
laws.statement: theorem nothing_back_falls {a p c : Nat} {pos : 0 < a} (cost : 0 < c) {x : CarrierCounts} (some : 0 < x.carrier) (n : Nat) : (Law.orbit (fun y => CarrierCounts.select y (shaped a 0 p c pos)) x (n + 1)).carrier * (Law.orbit ... x n).other < (Law.orbit ... x n).carrier * (Law.orbit ... x (n + 1)).other
laws.says: With s = 0, a positive cost and shapers present at the start, the shapers' share falls strictly at every step of the run under that one fixed rule. Their number does not fall: by `present_along` (RuleShaping.lean:271) they stay present for ever. Nothing ends and nothing is used up.

laws.name: RuleShaping.grouped_rises_iff
laws.statement: theorem grouped_rises_iff {gs : List (List α)} {w shapes : α → Nat} {a s q c m : Nat} {pos : 0 < a} (equal : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → g.length = m) (grouped : Grouped gs w shapes a s q c pos) : discord (whole gs) w shapes < concord (whole gs) w shapes ↔ c * concord (whole gs) shapes shapes < s * concord (whole gs) shapes shapes + m * q * concordAmong gs shapes shapes
laws.says: In groups of equal size m, where each member's offspring are as `Grouped` says (the group's shared part is q per shaper in it), offspring go with shaping more than against it exactly where c times the spread of shaping is below s times it plus m q times the spread among groups. One step, weights given; no level, no flow, no later step.

laws.name: RuleShaping.grouped_alike_iff / grouped_uniform_iff
laws.statement: grouped_alike_iff (equal) (grouped) (alike : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → total g shapes = d) (varies : 0 < concord (whole gs) shapes shapes) : discord (whole gs) w shapes < concord (whole gs) w shapes ↔ c < s; grouped_uniform_iff (equal) (grouped) (uniform : ∀ g, g ∈ gs → ∃ v, ∀ x, x ∈ g → shapes x = v) (differ : 0 < concordAmong gs shapes shapes) : ... ↔ c < s + m * q
laws.says: With every group holding the same number of shapers the verdict is c < s whatever is shared; with each group all shapers or none it is c < s + m q. These are the two ends D6's two arrangements resemble, at one step and with no condition that can run out.

laws.name: D5 check: giving back against taking less, five readings of a step
laws.statement: Units (h, b) with 0 ≤ b ≤ h ≤ 4, ways of up to 3 units, small levels. S0 (Flow.Balances): level differs 0, feasibility differs 0 of 75,915; takers differ in 45,192, renewers, uptake and replenishment in 72,660. S1 (RegimeMargin.step with hump10, giving back added): differs in 35,613 of 39,765, of which 10,100 not overdrawn. S2 (constant source): differs in 77,865 of 97,605, none with Σh ≤ x. S3 (takers in order): who is met differs in 13,472 (giving back at once) and 18,695 (at the end) of 25,305. S4 (need read after takes, before giving back): differs in 825 of 2,790; read at the start: 0.
laws.says: Giving back equals taking less for the level under balance with no order inside the step, by the definition. It differs in the package's counts, in November's step (cut-off subtraction, and a giving read after the take), and wherever takers are served in order or a need is read between take and giving back.

laws.name: D6 model, arrangement (i): each line its own second condition
laws.where: /Users/ren/theories/tmp/r7/one-model/check/round16/search/refute/d6_model.py (results: d6_analysis.txt, d6_analysis2.txt in the same folder)
laws.statement: Kinds G, T; first condition(s) A fed by one source giving s per step; each unit takes hX from A (hG = hT + ch), each met G gives b ≤ hG to its second condition; each met unit asks kX offspring, each taking r from its line's second condition (or, threshold mode, requiring it to stand at 1). Grid: s 1-4, A0 0/6, hT 1/2, ch 0/1, b 1/2, (kG,kT) (1,1)/(1,2)/(2,2), r 1/2 or threshold, B0 0/2/8, shared or own A, order of service G first / T first / proportional, gift before or after, starts (1,1),(2,2),(1,3),(3,1). Taking mode, 32,256 runs: T ends in every run (by step floor(B0/r)+1); G for ever and T ends 9,837; both end 22,419. G alone for ever exactly where s ≥ hG, b ≥ r and (B0 ≥ r or gift before). Given that, with T present (equal starts): own A 1,680/1,680 G goes on; shared A, G first 1,680/1,680; T first 709/1,680; proportional 934/1,680. Threshold mode, 16,128 runs: T for ever in 6,432, T for ever while G ends in 3,568.
laws.says: The non-giving line ends by its own doing only because its offspring use up a standing nothing renews; where the standing is only required it never ends. The giving line goes on only if its gift covers its offspring's take and the other line cannot starve it on a shared first condition; with own first conditions the two lines never affect each other (0 of 8,064 runs).

laws.name: D6 model, arrangement (ii): one second condition shared by both lines
laws.statement: Same model and grid. Taking mode, 96,768 runs: T for ever after G ends 0; G for ever and T ends 14,144 (8,986 with G served first from B; 2,226 with T served first from B, none of those at equal starts with kT = 2 unless G is served first from A; 2,932 proportional, all from unequal starts); both for ever 2,072; both end 80,552 (G first 30,545, same step 41,322, T first 8,685). No priority and equal starts, 8,064 runs: G for ever and T ends 0; cost in offspring (kG < kT) 2,688 runs, both end in all; no cost 2,304 runs, identical fates in all; cost only in what G takes 3,072 runs, both for ever in 184. Pooling the same parameters from (i) to (ii) under proportional shares: G for ever becomes G ends in 6,264 runs, T ends becomes T for ever in 677, G ends becomes G for ever in 36.
laws.says: With what is given coming back in proportion to what is asked and giving costing offspring, the giver is never the line left and both end; the taker never survives the giver. Giving is favoured outright when the giver is served first from the shared condition, and both lines go on for ever when the cost is not a cost in offspring.

laws.name: D6 model, check of the for-ever verdicts
laws.statement: 1,237 of the 65,540 runs with a for-ever verdict rerun for 3,000 steps with the repeat proof switched off: 0 mismatches. The proof used: counts equal to an earlier state and each level equal to it, or higher while not binding at any step between.
laws.says: Every for-ever verdict is a repeat of the counts, so every line that goes on does so at a bounded size; none grows without bound.

The frozen picture is drawn wrong in four places, by the Lean and by the model.

1. "An amount that stays when nobody touches it ... October's Lean does not allow that." It is the other way round. `Balances` (Flow.lean:278) with nothing taken and nothing given is `level (t+1) c = level t c`: an untouched amount stays, by definition. `Cycle.web` has `level _ _ := 1` for ever. Balance forbids only a rise with nothing given and a fall with nothing taken (Flow.lean:519, 531).

2. "Grows by a rule of its own ... not made by anything going on." Balance does not make a giver be made of anything. `Growing` (Flow.lean:775-787) is one formation that takes nothing, requires nothing, and gives 1 at every step. "A sun or a river is then one of the formations" is Arising.lean:22, said of `RenewedBy`, and the same paragraph adds that what `renews` means "left unconstrained ... says nothing". So October's difference from `RegimeMargin.step` is that the giver is listed in `present`, not that nothing comes from nowhere. The premise that does constrain a giver is `Dissipative` (Dissipation.lean:242-249), and its law runs against the picture: `Dissipative.opens` (Dissipation.lean:452) says a family taken from again and again is in no finite family that stays closed, so an outside always remains.

3. Requiring is not taking. `Supported` (Dependence.lean:134) and `LineOnAStock.Goes` (LineOnAStock.lean:150) are thresholds on a level; `Flow.take` and `use` are separate. D6 reads "requires" as "uses up". In the threshold reading its first half fails outright (T for ever in 6,432 of 16,128 runs), and the package's general ending law (`unfed_consumption_ends_at`) has taking as a premise.

4. Where giving lands is not which condition it lands on. In the model one shared condition with the giver served first returns the gift to the giver alone (G for ever, T ends, 8,986 runs), and two own second conditions with a shared first condition let the non-giver end the giver (971 of 1,680 with T served first). What decides is who gets back what was given and who is short of what, which is a matter of the order of access and of shortage on each level, neither of which the picture or `RuleShaping` has.

On the three questions asked.
- A bounded source: in the model every met unit takes at least 1 from A and only the source gives to A, so the number of met units over N steps is at most A0 + sN. No way grows without bound, and all 65,540 for-ever verdicts are repeats at bounded size: the units multiply and the excess goes unmet each step. In the Lean this is `Balances.replenished_over`, but only where nothing except the source gives to the family; `Cycle.closed_more` is more without end with no source at all, the takers giving back. So "a bounded source allows only bounded ways" needs the premise that the units do not give back to what they take from, or dissipation.
- The same first condition: with own first conditions and own second conditions the lines are two separate worlds (G's verdict equals G alone in all 8,064 runs), so nothing is selected. With a shared first condition the non-giver's private standing B0 works as an inheritance that lets it outgrow and starve the giver before it ends itself; pooling the second conditions then rescues the giver in 328 runs by taking that inheritance away.
- Whole numbers: under proportional shares a rare line can be rounded to nothing in one step whatever it gives (174 runs from (3,1) with a cost in offspring where G goes on and T ends; from (1,3) T outlasts G in 1,773 runs against 29). `RuleShaping`'s multiplied counts cannot show this.

D6's selection half is `favours_iff` with its premises; its ending half is nowhere in `RuleShaping`, where a disfavoured kind keeps multiplying for ever at a falling share. A join would have to make the offspring counts a + s + p and a + c + p come from levels, and the model says the shared part p then depends on the order of access and on how many givers are present, which `shaped` holds constant (the module says so itself, RuleShaping.lean:119-121).

So 'a cut-off course' is not a break: after the net ends the way is [] and the level goes on as x ↦ x + giving x.

Flow.give takes the step as an argument, so 'giving of what is left after the take' is just the number recorded at step t. Balances has no order inside a step, so 'step gives after the take' is not a break either.

variable {U : Type} (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat)

def dependence : Dependence (List U × Nat) (Option U) Unit where
  level s _ := s.2
  active s f := match f with | some u => u ∈ s.1 | none => True
  requires _ f _ := match f with | some _ => True | none => False
  need _ f _ := match f with | some u => need u | none => 0

def flow (s : List U × Nat) : Flow (Option U) Unit where

  give t f _ := match f with

theorem flow_balances_iff (s : List U × Nat) :

    (flow need kids giving use s).Balances (web need kids giving use s)

theorem flow_acting_taking (s : List U × Nat) :
    (flow need kids giving use s).Acting (web need kids giving use s) ∧
      (flow need kids giving use s).Taking (web need kids giving use s)

laws.name: Dependence, Web, Flow, World
laws.statement: structure Dependence (S : Type u) (F C : Type) where level : S → C → Nat; active : S → F → Prop; requires : S → F → C → Prop; need : S → F → C → Nat; draws : S → F → C → Prop. abbrev Web (F C : Type) := Dependence Nat F C. structure Flow (F C : Type) where present : Nat → List F; take : Nat → F → C → Nat; give : Nat → F → C → Nat. structure World where Relatum : Type; history : Run (everyStep (WebAt Relatum) (Exchange Relatum))
laws.says: Records only. A web is levels, activity, requirement, need and drawing per step; a flow is a list of formations taking part per step and what each takes from and gives to each condition. No field ties one to another, and `present` is not asked to be without repetition.

laws.name: Flow.taken, Flow.given, Flow.Balances
laws.statement: def taken (t : Nat) (c : C) : Nat := total (L.present t) fun f => L.take t f c; def given (t : Nat) (c : C) : Nat := total (L.present t) fun f => L.give t f c; def Balances (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t c, W.level (t + 1) c + L.taken t c = W.level t c + L.given t c
laws.says: Balance is one equation of totals per step and condition. It has no order inside the step, does not ask that a giver take anything, and does not bound what is taken by what stood before.

laws.name: Flow.Acting, Flow.Taking, Web.Supported, Web.Dependent
laws.statement: def Acting (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t f c, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.give t f c → W.active t f; def Taking (W : Web F C) : Prop := ∀ t f c, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < L.take t f c → W.active t f ∧ W.draws t f c; def Supported (t : Nat) (f : F) : Prop := ∀ c, W.requires t f c → W.need t f c ≤ W.level t c; def Dependent : Prop := ∀ t f, W.active t f → W.Supported t f
laws.says: Premises stated where used, not fields. Together `Taking` and `Dependent` say that whatever takes at a step is supported at that same step, which the line's unmet unit that still takes does not meet.

laws.name: Flow.takers, Flow.renewers, Flow.More, Flow.Capacity
laws.statement: def takers (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Nat := count (L.present t) fun f => total cs (L.take t f); def renewers … (L.give t f); def More (cs : List C) : Prop := ∀ K, ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → K ≤ L.takers cs t; def Capacity (cs : List C) (g : Nat) : Prop := ∀ t f, f ∈ L.present t → total cs (L.give t f) ≤ g
laws.says: `More` counts entries of `present` with a positive take, with repetition; it is about how many take, not how much is taken.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.over, Flow.Balances.accumulates
laws.statement: theorem Balances.over (balances : L.Balances W) : ∀ (cs : List C) (t : Nat), W.stock cs (t + 1) + L.uptake cs t = W.stock cs t + L.replenishment cs t; theorem Balances.accumulates (balances : L.Balances W) (cs : List C) : ∀ T N, W.stock cs (T + N) + total (steps T N) (L.uptake cs) = W.stock cs T + total (steps T N) (L.replenishment cs)
laws.says: A balanced family's total after a stretch, with everything taken, is its total before with everything given. Through `accumulates_on` (:505) it is `balance_over_stretch_on` of Prelude, the same lemma `LineOnAStock.account` instantiates.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.rise_given, Flow.Balances.renewedBy, Flow.Balances.fall_taken, Flow.Balances.takenBy
laws.statement: theorem Balances.rise_given (balances : L.Balances W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (rises : W.Rises t c) : 0 < L.given t c; theorem Balances.renewedBy (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) : W.RenewedBy fun t f c => f ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.give t f c; theorem Balances.fall_taken (balances : L.Balances W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (falls : W.Falls t c) : 0 < L.taken t c; theorem Balances.takenBy (balances : L.Balances W) (taking : L.Taking W) {t : Nat} {c : C} (falls : W.Falls t c) : ∃ f, f ∈ L.present t ∧ 0 < L.take t f c ∧ W.active t f ∧ W.draws t f c
laws.says: In a balanced flow every rise is given to and every fall taken from by some listed formation. This is the sense in which 'every change is the work of a formation'; it holds trivially of a named giver that takes nothing.

laws.name: Flow.uptake_needs_replenishment
laws.statement: theorem uptake_needs_replenishment {cs : List C} (balances : L.Balances W) (uptake : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.uptake cs t) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.replenishment cs t = 0
laws.says: In a balanced flow, taking at arbitrarily late steps needs giving at some step after any step. One-directional; needs only balance.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.replenished_over, Flow.More.replenishment_unbounded, Flow.More.renewers_unbounded
laws.statement: theorem Balances.replenished_over {cs : List C} {K S : Nat} (balances : L.Balances W) (many : ∀ t, S ≤ t → K ≤ L.takers cs t) (N : Nat) : K * N ≤ W.stock cs S + total (steps S N) (L.replenishment cs); theorem More.replenishment_unbounded {cs : List C} (balances : L.Balances W) (more : L.More cs) (R T₀ : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.replenishment cs t ≤ R; theorem More.renewers_unbounded {cs : List C} {g : Nat} (balances : L.Balances W) (capacity : L.Capacity cs g) (more : L.More cs) (M T₀ : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.renewers cs t ≤ M
laws.says: With balance and ever more takers, no bound holds of what the family is given from any step on; with each formation giving at most g, none holds of how many give. Proved from `Amounts.replenishment_unbounded`, using the takers only as a lower bound on the uptake.

laws.name: Amounts.replenishment_unbounded
laws.statement: theorem replenishment_unbounded (archimedean : M.Archimedean) {s u r : Nat → A} {ε : A} {T₀ : Nat} (positive : ¬ M.le ε M.zero) (balances : ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → M.le (M.add (s (t + 1)) (u t)) (M.add (s t) (r t))) (more : ∀ m, ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → M.le (M.times m ε) (u t)) (b : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → M.le (r t) (M.times b ε)
laws.says: The law under `More.replenishment_unbounded`: a stock balanced from T₀ on whose uptake is eventually above every multiple of a least take is replenished beyond every such multiple. This, not `More`, is the form a growing line could meet.

laws.name: Growing.growing
laws.statement: theorem growing : flow.Balances web ∧ (∀ t, web.Rises t ()) ∧ (∀ t, ¬ web.ComesToStand t ()) ∧ ∀ t, 0 < flow.given t ()
laws.says: A condition that rises by one at every step, one formation giving it one unit and taking nothing, balances. Balance alone admits an amount that grows by a named giver with no source.

laws.name: Expansion.more, Steady.steady, Oscillation.not_more, Pulse.pulsed
laws.statement: Expansion.more : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ t, web.Arises t (.renewer, t)) ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ flow.More [()]. Steady.steady : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ (∀ t, 0 < flow.uptake [()] t) ∧ (∀ t f, ¬ web.Arises t f) ∧ ∀ T, ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → flow.replenishment [()] t = 0. Oscillation.not_more : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ¬ flow.More [()]. Pulse.pulsed : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ ∀ T, ∃ t, T ≤ t ∧ flow.renewers [()] t = 0 ∧ flow.replenishment [()] t = 0
laws.says: Four balanced flows on one condition, each with renewers that give and take nothing. In Expansion the level is 1 for ever while t growers each take one across step t: more is taken across a step than stood before it.

laws.name: Cycle.closed_more
laws.statement: theorem closed_more : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ flow.Capacity [()] 1 ∧ web.Dependent ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ (∀ t, web.stock [()] (t + 1) = web.stock [()] t) ∧ ∀ t, flow.renewers [()] t = flow.takers [()] t
laws.says: On one condition held at 1, formation n arises at step n and each takes one and gives one back across the same step; more without end, the total never changing. Not dissipative (`witnesses_not_dissipative`).

laws.name: Flow.ClosedAt, Flow.DissipatesOn, Flow.Dissipative, Flow.Enclosed, Flow.Around, Flow.Inward
laws.statement: def ClosedAt (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Prop := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → ∀ c, ¬ c ∈ cs → L.take t f c = 0 ∧ L.give t f c = 0; def DissipatesOn (cs : List C) (t : Nat) : Prop := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → total cs (L.give t f) + sign (total cs (L.take t f)) ≤ total cs (L.take t f); def Dissipative : Prop := ∀ cs t, Distinct cs → L.ClosedAt cs t → L.DissipatesOn cs t; def Enclosed (t : Nat) : Prop := ∃ cs, Distinct cs ∧ L.ClosedAt cs t; def Around (ds : List C) (t : Nat) : Prop := ∃ es, Distinct es ∧ (∀ c, c ∈ ds → c ∈ es) ∧ L.ClosedAt es t; def Inward (ds : List C) (t : Nat) : Prop := ∀ f, f ∈ L.present t → 0 < total ds (L.give t f) → ∀ c, 0 < L.take t f c → c ∈ ds
laws.says: Dissipation is the premise that, per formation, what it gives a closed family is no more than it takes from it, and one less when it takes. This, not balance, is what refuses a giver from nowhere.

laws.name: Flow.Dissipative.giving_needs_uptake
laws.statement: theorem Dissipative.giving_needs_uptake (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {t : Nat} (enclosed : L.Enclosed t) {f : F} (present : f ∈ L.present t) {c : C} (gives : 0 < L.give t f c) : ∃ d, 0 < L.take t f d
laws.says: Under dissipation, across a step whose exchange lies within finitely many conditions, a formation that gives takes from some condition. No balance needed.

laws.name: Flow.Balances.runs_down, Flow.Balances.takers_within, Flow.Balances.taking_not_recurring
laws.statement: theorem Balances.runs_down (balances : L.Balances W) {cs : List C} {t : Nat} (dissipates : L.DissipatesOn cs t) : W.stock cs (t + 1) + L.takers cs t ≤ W.stock cs t; theorem Balances.takers_within (balances : L.Balances W) {cs : List C} : ∀ S N, (∀ t, S ≤ t → L.DissipatesOn cs t) → W.stock cs (S + N) + total (steps S N) (L.takers cs) ≤ W.stock cs S; theorem Balances.taking_not_recurring (balances : L.Balances W) {cs : List C} {T : Nat} (dissipates : ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.DissipatesOn cs t) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers cs t
laws.says: A balanced family dissipated on falls by at least its number of takers per step, so all its later takers number at most its stock and taking from it stops recurring.

laws.name: Flow.Dissipative.opens, Flow.Dissipative.finite_taking_not_recurring, Flow.More.opens
laws.statement: theorem Dissipative.opens (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {cs ds : List C} (distinct : Distinct ds) (within : ∀ c, c ∈ cs → c ∈ ds) (recurs : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers cs t) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.ClosedAt ds t; theorem Dissipative.finite_taking_not_recurring (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {all : List C} (distinct : Distinct all) (every : ∀ c, c ∈ all) (cs : List C) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers cs t; theorem More.opens (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {cs ds : List C} (distinct : Distinct ds) (within : ∀ c, c ∈ cs → c ∈ ds) (more : L.More cs) (T : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → L.ClosedAt ds t
laws.says: Balanced and dissipative, any taking that recurs (growing or not) keeps every finite family around it open; where finitely many conditions are all there is, taking does not recur at all.

laws.name: Flow.taking_draws_in
laws.statement: theorem taking_draws_in (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) {ds : List C} (distinct : Distinct ds) {T₀ : Nat} (around : ∀ t, T₀ ≤ t → L.Around ds t) (recurs : ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers ds t) (N : Nat) : ¬ ∀ t, N ≤ t → L.Inward ds t
laws.says: Balanced, dissipative and enclosed around the family from some step on, recurring taking from it needs, at some step after any step, a formation that gives to it and takes from a condition beyond it: the source is said.

laws.name: Flow.rise_with_fall, Flow.rise_exchange
laws.statement: theorem rise_with_fall (balances : L.Balances W) {ds : List C} {t : Nat} (dissipates : L.DissipatesOn ds t) {c : C} (mem : c ∈ ds) (rises : W.Rises t c) : ∃ d, d ∈ ds ∧ d ≠ c ∧ W.Falls t d; theorem rise_exchange (balances : L.Balances W) (acting : L.Acting W) (taking : L.Taking W) {ds : List C} {t : Nat} (dissipates : L.DissipatesOn ds t) {c : C} (mem : c ∈ ds) (rises : W.Rises t c) : (∃ f, f ∈ L.present t ∧ W.active t f ∧ 0 < L.give t f c ∧ 0 < total ds (L.take t f)) ∧ ∃ d g, d ∈ ds ∧ d ≠ c ∧ W.Falls t d ∧ g ∈ L.present t ∧ W.active t g ∧ W.draws t g d ∧ 0 < L.take t g d
laws.says: In a family dissipated on, a member rises only while another member falls across the same step, and an active formation gives to the one and takes from the family. The nearest general statement here of one condition made out of another.

laws.name: Flow.Dissipative.one_taking_not_recurring, witnesses_not_dissipative
laws.statement: theorem Flow.Dissipative.one_taking_not_recurring {F : Type} {L : Flow F Unit} {W : Web F Unit} (balances : L.Balances W) (dissipative : L.Dissipative) : ¬ ∀ N, ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ 0 < L.takers [()] t; theorem witnesses_not_dissipative : ¬ Expansion.flow.Dissipative ∧ ¬ Cycle.flow.Dissipative ∧ ¬ Pulse.flow.Dissipative ∧ ¬ Steady.flow.Dissipative ∧ ¬ Repeated.flow.Dissipative ∧ ¬ Oscillation.flow.Dissipative
laws.says: The first is general: on one condition a balanced flow in which taking recurs is not dissipative. The second applies it to six built flows. A line's course recorded on one condition falls under the first whenever it goes on taking.

laws.name: Frontier (flow, dissipative, more, frontier, draws_in, gives_without_taking), Rooted.rooted, Lone.lone, Spray.spray
laws.statement: Rooted.rooted : Frontier.flow.Balances web ∧ Frontier.flow.Acting web ∧ Frontier.flow.Taking web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ web.Census Frontier.flow.present ∧ Frontier.flow.Dissipative ∧ Frontier.flow.More [.pool] ∧ web.Unceasing ∧ ∀ {ds : List Condition}, Distinct ds → Condition.pool ∈ ds → ∀ T, ¬ ∀ t, T ≤ t → Frontier.flow.ClosedAt ds t. Lone.lone : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ (∀ t, flow.takers [.pool] t = 1) ∧ (∀ t f, ¬ web.Arises t f) ∧ ¬ flow.More [.pool]. Spray.spray : flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ web.Dependent ∧ flow.Dissipative ∧ (∀ t, ¬ flow.Enclosed t) ∧ (∀ t, 0 < flow.give t .renewer 0 ∧ ∀ c, flow.take t .renewer c = 0) ∧ ∀ t, 0 < flow.takers [0] t
laws.says: Frontier/Rooted: a source burns a fresh fuel (t + 1 units) at each step and gives a pool t, while t growers that depend on the pool each take one; every premise including dissipation holds, with infinitely many conditions. Lone: one eater kept for ever already needs the same. Spray: where no step is enclosed, dissipation holds emptily and a renewer gives from nothing.

laws.name: Stock.Balanced, Stock.DrawsHeld, Stock.process, Stock.Covered, Stock.along
laws.statement: def Balanced (P : Process S A) (σ : S → Nat) (draw replenish : A → Nat) : Prop := ∀ s a t, P.step s a t → σ t + draw a = σ s + replenish a; def DrawsHeld (P : Process S A) (σ : S → Nat) (draw : A → Nat) : Prop := ∀ s a t, P.step s a t → draw a ≤ σ s; def process (draw replenish : A → Nat) : Process Nat A := ⟨fun n a m => draw a ≤ n ∧ m + draw a = n + replenish a⟩; def along (draw replenish : A → Nat) (n : Nat) (acts : Nat → A) : Nat → Nat | 0 => n | k + 1 => along draw replenish n acts k - draw (acts k) + replenish (acts k)
laws.says: October's stock: a step draws from what is held, then replenishes. `along` is the same recursion as `RegimeMargin.step` (truncated subtraction, then add), with draw and replenishment read off an action.

laws.name: Stock.trace_balance, Stock.cycles_need, Stock.repeat_covered_iff, Stock.carried_iff, Run.replenishes_of_draws
laws.statement: theorem trace_balance {P : Process S A} {σ : S → Nat} {draw replenish : A → Nat} (bal : Balanced P σ draw replenish) {s t : S} {as : List A} (h : Trace P s as t) : σ t + total as draw = σ s + total as replenish; theorem cycles_need (bal : Balanced P σ draw replenish) {s : S} {w : Nat → List A} {D R : Nat} (drawn : ∀ k, total (w k) draw = D) (renewed : ∀ k, total (w k) replenish = R) (each : ∀ k, Feasible P s (cycles w k)) : D ≤ R; theorem repeat_covered_iff {draw replenish : A → Nat} {w : List A} {n : Nat} : (∀ k, Covered draw replenish n (repeatCourse w k)) ↔ Covered draw replenish n w ∧ total w draw ≤ total w replenish; theorem carried_iff {S' : Type u} {R : Process S' A} {draw replenish : A → Nat} (r : Run R) (n : Nat) : (∃ q : Run (productProcess (process draw replenish) R), (q.state 0).1 = n ∧ (∀ k, (q.state k).2 = r.state k) ∧ ∀ k, q.act k = r.act k) ↔ ∀ k, draw (r.act k) ≤ along draw replenish n r.act k; theorem Run.replenishes_of_draws (bal : Stock.Balanced P σ draw replenish) (r : Run P) (draws : ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ 0 < draw (r.act n)) : ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ 0 < replenish (r.act n)
laws.says: For every balanced process: totals balance along every course; a course repeated without end must replenish at least what it draws, and exactly that with a covered first pass for the stock process; an unending course is carried by a stock exactly where each draw is within what then stands; drawing that recurs needs replenishment that recurs.

laws.name: Run.stockFlow, Run.stockWeb, Run.stockFlow_balances_iff, Run.stockFlow_balances
laws.statement: def stockFlow {P : Process S A} (r : Run P) (draw replenish : A → Nat) : Flow Unit Unit := ⟨fun _ => [()], fun t _ _ => draw (r.act t), fun t _ _ => replenish (r.act t)⟩; def stockWeb {P : Process S A} (r : Run P) (σ : S → Nat) : Web Unit Unit := ⟨fun t _ => σ (r.state t), fun _ _ => True, fun _ _ _ => False, fun _ _ _ => 0, fun _ _ _ => True⟩; theorem stockFlow_balances_iff {P : Process S A} (r : Run P) (σ : S → Nat) (draw replenish : A → Nat) : (stockFlow r draw replenish).Balances (stockWeb r σ) ↔ ∀ n, σ (r.state (n + 1)) + draw (r.act n) = σ (r.state n) + replenish (r.act n)
laws.says: Any stock balanced along a run is a balanced flow on one condition, with one formation that both takes the step's draw and gives its replenishment. General, in the package since October, and used by no module but Stock.

laws.name: RegimeMargin.step, FromNothing, Short, Meets, Keeps
laws.statement: def step (g : Nat → Nat) (H x : Nat) : Nat := (x - H) + g (x - H); def FromNothing (g : Nat → Nat) : Prop := g 0 = 0; def Short (g : Nat → Nat) (H y : Nat) : Prop := ∀ z, z < y → g z < H; def Meets (g : Nat → Nat) (H y hi : Nat) : Prop := ∀ z, y ≤ z → z + H ≤ hi → H ≤ g z; def Keeps (g : Nat → Nat) (H hi : Nat) : Prop := ∀ x, x ≤ hi → step g H x ≤ hi
laws.says: The draw takes first, as much as there is, and the level gives g of what is left; no formation gives. First committed 20 October. Where H > x the step is not a balance of H taken against g given.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.after, taken, left, Goes, step, net, course, generation
laws.statement: def after (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) : List U → Nat → List U | [], _ => [] | u :: w, x => cond (decide (need u ≤ x)) (kids u) [] ++ after need kids w x; def taken (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) : Nat := total w use; def left (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) (x : Nat) : Nat := RegimeMargin.step giving (taken use w) x; def Goes (need : U → Nat) (s : List U × Nat) : Prop := ∃ u, u ∈ s.1 ∧ need u ≤ s.2; abbrev step … := TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) (left giving use); def net … := Law.stepWhile (Goes need) (step need kids giving use); abbrev course … (s) : Nat → List U × Nat := Law.orbit (step need kids giving use) s; def generation (kids : U → List U) : Nat → List U → List U | 0, w => w | n + 1, w => allKids kids (generation kids n w)
laws.says: Every unit present takes its use whether its need is met or not; a unit met at the level leaves its kids, an unmet one nothing. The course is a total orbit; only the net is cut where no need is met. A way may list one unit several times.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.account, LineOnAStock.unending_taken_below
laws.statement: theorem account {s : List U × Nat} (N : Nat) (within : ∀ t, t < N → taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1 ≤ (course need kids giving use s t).2) : (course need kids giving use s N).2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1) = s.2 + total (steps 0 N) (fun t => giving ((course need kids giving use s t).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use s t).1)); theorem unending_taken_below (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) {s : List U × Nat} (needs : Needing need kids s.1) (never : «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» s) (n : Nat) : taken use (course need kids giving use s n).1 < (course need kids giving use s n).2
laws.says: The line's own balance over a stretch, under the premise that the take is within the level at each step; and that premise holds, strictly, at every step of a net that never ends when nothing is given from nothing and every descendant needs something.

laws.name: LineOnAStock.way_ends, LineOnAStock.need_unmet
laws.statement: theorem way_ends {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi) (grows : ∀ u, use u < taken use (kids u)) (needs : ∀ u, 0 < need u) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) : (∃ n, ¬ Goes need (course need kids giving use (w, x) n)) ∧ ¬ «不穷» (net need kids giving use) «一» (w, x); need_unmet: same `nothing`, `keeps`, `grows`, with `needs : Needing need kids w`, `high`, `ne : w ≠ []`, `met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x`, concluding ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ hi + 1 ∧ (every need met before n) ∧ (the way at each j ≤ n is generation kids j w) ∧ some unit at n has its need unmet
laws.says: A way all of whose units' kids take more ends on a stock whose level is capped at hi, with the further premises named. The arithmetic is a take rising against a capped level that it cannot exceed without leaving nothing; that cap on a step's take is not a consequence of `Flow.Balances`.

laws.name: ReadOffInTime.FourReaders.flow, web, balances, stopped_is_regime
laws.statement: theorem balances : ∀ k, (flow k).Balances (web k); theorem stopped_is_regime : ∀ k n, habitat k (n + stopAt k) = (Law.run (RegimeMargin.step giving 1) (habitat k (stopAt k))).state n; with def giving (z : Nat) : Nat := if 1 ≤ z then 1 else 0 (:1025) and, in `flow`, take t .dweller .habitat := if 1 ≤ habitat k t then 1 else 0, give t .renewer .habitat := if 2 ≤ habitat k t then 1 else 0, take t .renewer _ := 0
laws.says: On four built courses a condition's level on a balanced flow is, once a clearer stops, the regime's run under a draw of one; the regime's giving is a formation `renewer` that gives and takes nothing. The carrying D4 proposes, done once by hand.

laws.name: Repeated.more_without_arising, Flow.More.unceasing
laws.statement: theorem more_without_arising : web.Census (fun _ => [()]) ∧ flow.Balances web ∧ flow.Acting web ∧ flow.Taking web ∧ flow.More [()] ∧ ¬ (∀ t, Distinct (flow.present t)) ∧ ∀ t f, ¬ web.Arises t f (flow := ⟨rep, fun _ _ _ => 1, fun _ _ _ => 1⟩, listing the one formation t times); theorem Flow.More.unceasing {W : Web F C} [∀ t f, Decidable (W.active t f)] {L : Flow F C} {cs : List C} {alive : Nat → List F} (census : W.Census alive) (distinct : ∀ t, Distinct (L.present t)) (taking : L.Taking W) (more : L.More cs) : W.Unceasing
laws.says: The first is a built example: a flow may list one formation many times and still balance and be more without end, and then nothing need arise. The second is a general law (reported here beside it because it is the one the example bounds): with a census, each formation listed once and only active formations taking, more takers without end make arising unceasing. A way that lists a unit several times is on the first side.

laws.name: Dependence.along
laws.statement: def Dependence.along (K : Dependence S F C) {P : Process S A} (r : Run P) : Web F C := ⟨fun t => K.level (r.state t), fun t => K.active (r.state t), fun t => K.requires (r.state t), fun t => K.need (r.state t), fun t => K.draws (r.state t)⟩
laws.says: A dependence on configurations read along a run is a web. With `Law.run (LineOnAStock.step …) s` this gives the web side of the carrying with nothing new defined.

v2:29e663f04f399ded4d89a73733ce0997d6a76.beyond_the_guesses:
AI-written (reader web-base). Six things the guesses do not expect, or where the frozen file's picture is drawn wrong.

1. THE PICTURE 'OCTOBER'S LEAN DOES NOT ALLOW THAT' IS WRONG FOR BALANCE. The frozen file says an amount that 'grows by a rule of its own is not made by anything going on. October's Lean does not allow that: on its web a change of a level is what the goings-on present take and give (`Flow.Balances`)'. `Balances` asks only that a giver be listed. `Growing.growing` (Flow.lean:784) is a balanced flow whose one formation gives one unit a step and takes nothing; so are the renewers of Steady, Expansion, Oscillation, Pulse and Spray. The sentence quoted from the Flow header ('a sun or a river is then one of the formations, not an outside') is exactly that: naming the outside as a formation. What refuses a giver from nowhere is `Dissipative` across an enclosed step (`giving_needs_uptake`, Dissipation.lean:316), which Dissipation.lean:101-102 calls a physical premise and which `witnesses_not_dissipative` (:1369) proves six of October's own flows fail. So the line between the two months is not balance. It is whether the giver's source is said, and October says it in one family of built examples only (Frontier, Rooted, Lone), by a fresh condition burned at every step.

2. BY OCTOBER'S MEASURE THE LEVEL'S OWN GIVING WAS ALREADY FROM NOWHERE IN EVERY COURSE OF THE LINE THAT GOES ON, not only in the tried `give`. Recorded on one condition, any course that keeps taking is balanced and so not dissipative (`Flow.Dissipative.one_taking_not_recurring`, Dissipation.lean:1361, a general law). That covers the holding regime (`Holds`, `unending_iff_holds`) as much as the morning's growing way; growth adds nothing to it. And under dissipation October's law is stronger than 'two conditions': no finite family stays closed (`Dissipative.opens`, :452; `finite_taking_not_recurring`, :461).

3. THE NEAREST OCTOBER OBJECT TO THE LINE'S LEVEL IS `Stock`, NOT `Flow`, AND THE LINE DOES NOT USE IT. `Stock.process` (Stock.lean:120) is 'a step draws what it draws from what is held, then replenishes'; `Stock.along` (:492) is the same recursion as `RegimeMargin.step`; `Stock.Covered`/`carried_iff` (:110, :499) is the premise `within` of `LineOnAStock.account`; `trace_balance` (:78) is `account`'s content; `cycles_need`/`repeat_covered_iff` (:276, :319) are the law that a course repeated without end must replenish at least what it draws; and `Run.stockFlow_balances_iff` (:475) is already the bridge to a balanced flow. `LineOnAStock`, `WayOfUnits`, `TurningInTime` and `RegimeMargin` contain no reference to `Becoming.Stock` (grep). So a join that could shorten something is more likely Stock-to-line than web-to-line; I did not measure it.

4. THE WEB IS A RECORD AND THE LINE IS A LAW. `Flow.give : Nat → F → C → Nat` is a number per step; nothing on a `Flow` or `Web` can say that giving is a function of what is left, or that one formation descends from another. The premises the line's laws live on (`FromNothing`, `Keeps`, `Short`, `Meets` on g; `grows`, `down`, `closed` on kids) have no place on the web. D4's 'the line's laws are laws of a case of the web' therefore cannot come out as stated whichever way the carrying is done: what can come out is that each course of the line has a balanced record, and the web's laws under `Balances` hold of that record. October does have a law-governed web with no formations at all: `RegimeMargin.Coupled.Indexed.step G H x := fun i => D.add (D.sub (x i) (H i)) (G i (left D H x))` (RegimeMargin.lean:2113), each condition giving by a law of what is left of all. That is where 'what one gives another rests on' is a law in the package, and it too is off `Flow.Balances` (I read only its definition and the header).

5. THE LINE'S ONE RESPONSE TO THE FALL HAS NO CLEAN PLACE ON THE WEB. An unmet unit is present, takes its use, and leaves nothing. On the web that is a formation taking while unsupported; `Taking` and `Dependent` cannot both hold at that step.
